{
  "abstract_verbatim": "We prove that every word-hyperbolic one-relator group is virtually compact special. Combined with the work of Kielak–Linton, this resolves Wise's virtual free-by-cyclic conjecture for hyperbolic one-relator groups: every such group is virtually free-by-cyclic, with the free kernel allowed to have infinite rank.",

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> We prove that every word-hyperbolic one-relator group is virtually compact special. Combined with the work of Kielak–Linton, this resolves Wise's virtual free-by-cyclic conjecture for hyperbolic one-relator groups: every such group is virtually free-by-cyclic, with the free kernel allowed to have infinite rank.

- **claim-one-relator-specialness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-main)): Let $X$ be finite, let $r\in F(X)$, and suppose that $$G=F(X)/\langle\!\langle r\rangle\!\rangle$$ is word-hyperbolic. Then $G$ is virtually compact special. More precisely, there are a finite-index subgroup $H\leq G$, a finite connected nonpositively curved cube complex $C$, and a finite simplicial graph $\Lambda$ such that $$\pi_1(C)\cong H \quad\text{and}\quad C\longrightarrow S_\Lambda$$ is a cubical local isometry to the Salvetti complex of the right-angled Artin group defined by $\Lambda$.
  - Explanation: Hyperbolicity guarantees a compact special finite cover with a finite Salvetti target.
- **claim-ascending-specialness-intro** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-ascending-intro)): Let $F$ be a finitely generated free group and let $\phi:F\to F$ be injective. If its ascending mapping torus $$F*_{\phi}=\langle F,t\mid t^{-1}ft=\phi(f),\ f\in F\rangle$$ is word-hyperbolic, then it is virtually compact special.
  - Explanation: Injective free-group ascending tori satisfy virtual compact specialness under hyperbolicity.
- **claim-compact-cubulation-toolkit** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-compact-toolkit)): 1. *A word-hyperbolic group acting properly and cocompactly on a CAT(0) cube complex is virtually compact special.* 2. *A hyperbolic group with a finite graph-of-groups decomposition whose edge groups are quasiconvex in the ambient group and whose vertex groups are hyperbolic VCS is VCS. The same applies to a finite hierarchy of such decompositions.* 3. *A compact special cube complex admits a cubical local isometry to a Salvetti complex. Its defining graph can be taken finite.
  - Explanation: Cubulation, ambient quasiconvex hierarchies, and finite Salvetti models supply the compact-special toolkit.
- **claim-primitive-reduction** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-primitive-reduction)): To prove Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a>, it suffices to prove that every torsion-free hyperbolic primitive extension group in the two forms of [[LintonHyperbolic2026](#ref-LintonHyperbolic2026), Section 5] is VCS.
  - Explanation: The primitive terminal cases suffice for the main theorem.
- **claim-filling-criterion** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-fill-criterion)): Let $G_*$ be a torsion-free hyperbolic group satisfying the following conditions.* 1. *$G_*$ is locally indicable, coherent, of type $F$, and has integral cohomological dimension at most two.* 2. *$G_*$ has a division ring $D(G_*)$ satisfying the subgroup-field hypotheses, and the chains of a finite classifying space become acyclic over $D(G_*)$.* 3. *There is a finite malnormal family $\{D_j\}$ of quasiconvex hyperbolic virtually compact special subgroups such that arbitrarily deep peripheral fillings $$G_*\longrightarrow Q_*$$ are hyperbolic and virtually compact special, and their inherited peripheral images are hyperbolic and virtually compact special.* *In <span class="upright">(iii)</span>, arbitrarily deep means that the peripheral kernels can avoid any prescribed finite subset of $\bigcup_j(D_j\setminus\{1\})$; the inherited peripheral structure is the one furnished by relative Dehn filling.* *Then a finite-index subgroup of $G_*$ is an extension of a finite-rank free group by $\mathbb Z$. Consequently $G_*$ is virtually compact special.
  - Explanation: Field acyclicity and arbitrarily deep good peripheral fillings yield virtual fibering with finite-rank free kernel.
- **claim-uniform-selective-hyperbolicity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fill-selective-hyp)): The depth in <a href="#fill:cofinite" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="fill:cofinite">[fill:cofinite]</a> can be chosen so that the following holds for every finite-index preimage $H\le G_*$ containing $K$. For any $H$-invariant subset of quotient peripheral apices, kill the rotations over its full inverse image among original cosets, and let $K_-\lhd H$ be their normal closure. Then $H/K_-$ is hyperbolic. The required depth is independent of the index of $H$ and of the chosen invariant subset.
  - Explanation: One initial depth works for every finite-index preimage and invariant apex selection.
- **claim-selective-cover-quotient** (construction, [source](#stmt-fill-selective)): Choose <a href="#fill:cofinite" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="fill:cofinite">[fill:cofinite]</a> sufficiently deep. Let $H_{\mathrm{given}}$ be a finite-index preimage in $G_*$, and let $\mathcal B\subset\mathcal A$ be finite. There is a further finite-index preimage $H\le H_{\mathrm{given}}$, normal in $H_{\mathrm{given}}$, such that, on retaining all factors indexed by the $H$-translates of $\mathcal B$ and killing the other factors, the group $$P=H/K_- \label{fill:selective-quotient}$$ is hyperbolic and virtually compact special. The natural map to $P$ is injective on $*_{a\in\mathcal B}R_a$.
  - Explanation: A normal finite-index refinement retains the prescribed kernel factors inside a hyperbolic compact-special quotient.
- **claim-bounded-wall-collapse** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fill-collapse)): The cubing $Y$ is proper, the projection $p$ is a quasi-isometry, and every cube of $Y$ lifts to a cube of $C$. For a vertex $v\in Y$, let $E_v\subset C$ be the intersection of the closed mid-halfspaces selected by its retained-wall orientations. For a cube $\sigma\subset Y$, put $$E_\sigma=\bigcap_{v\in\sigma^{(0)}}E_v. \label{fill:chambers}$$ These sets are nonempty bounded convex sets. A point mapping into an open cube $\sigma$ is within $\dim C$ of $E_\sigma$. Every retained branch image is either $R$-deep in a vertex chamber or $R$-far from it, after decreasing $R$ by a fixed dimensional margin. Every $E_\sigma$ with $\dim\sigma>0$ is $R$-far from all retained branch images, with the same convention.
  - Explanation: Deleting sparse walls preserves coarse geometry and produces bounded convex chambers.
- **claim-sheet-stability** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fill-sheets)): With the choices above, the following hold.* 1. *Enlarging the path tolerance from $r$ to $D$ does not change the equivalence relation on near points. Points at any fixed intermediate distance can be assigned consistently to sheets by connecting them to near points.* 2. *$B$ acts transitively on the sheets over each $E_\sigma$. If $\dim\sigma>0$, this action is free. The transitions from a cube to one of its positive-dimensional faces are bijections on sheets.* 3. *The stabilizer of a vertex sheet is generated by the stabilizers of the branch lifts accessible in that sheet. These are whole conjugates of retained factors in <a href="#fill:CL" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="fill:CL">[fill:CL]</a>. There are finitely many orbits of such accessible branch lifts under the sheet stabilizer.
  - Explanation: Collar stability controls sheet transitions and identifies vertex stabilizers as generated by whole retained factors.
- **claim-cubical-branched-model** (construction, [source](#stmt-fill-cubical)): The complex $\widetilde Y$ is CAT(0), the $P$-action is cocompact, and every hyperplane maps isomorphically under $q$ to a hyperplane of $Y$.
  - Explanation: The sheet complex is CAT(0), cocompact, and preserves individual hyperplanes.
- **claim-controlled-linearization** (construction, [source](#stmt-fill-linearize)): A rational expression over a coefficient ring in a division ring has a representation $pA^{-1}q$, where $A$ is a square polynomial matrix and $p,q$ are constant selectors. The entries of $A^{-1}$ can be given rational expressions using sums and products of the original subexpressions and their original inverses. In particular linearization introduces neither a larger nested inverse depth nor new bottom denominators on a maximal-depth inverse chain.
  - Explanation: Block matrix formulas linearize rational expressions without increasing inverse ancestry complexity.
- **claim-finite-inverse-descent** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fill-ancestry)): Let $J/K$ have a normal RFRS chain, and pull it back to $$J=H_0\ge H_1\ge\cdots,\qquad \bigcap_iH_i=K.$$ Let $N_i\lhd H_0$ be the preimage of the rational abelianization kernel of $H_i/K$, so $N_i\le H_{i+1}$. At each stage expand finitely many specified rational expressions for both signs of a character with kernel $N_i$, retain finitely many coefficients, restrict those scalar coefficient problems to $H_{i+1}$, and use Lemma <a href="#fill:linearize" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fill:linearize">12</a>. After finitely many stages the resulting coefficient problems have inverse depth zero over $D(K)$.
  - Explanation: Normal residual separation eventually lowers every surviving maximal inverse chain.
- **claim-character-recombination** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-fill-recombine)): Suppose a finite stage of the preceding procedure used a character $\chi_i$ on $H_i$. For each of its polynomial matrices $A$, fix finite homogeneous truncations $B_+,B_-$ of $A^{-1}$ such that $I-AB_\pm$ and $I-B_\pm A$ have strictly positive weights for $\pm\chi_i$, respectively. Suppose all scalar coefficients of the matrices $A,B_+,B_-$ have been realized, after restriction to a finite-index subgroup $F$, in both ordinary Novikov rings for a character $\psi$ of $F$, compatibly with their rational-field values. Then its original matrix inverse problems are realized for both signs of $$\chi_i\|_F+\epsilon\psi \label{fill:perturb}$$ for every sufficiently small positive $\epsilon$.
  - Explanation: Small positive perturbations reconstruct both Novikov realizations from realized coefficient problems.
- **claim-progressive-characters** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fill-progressive)): Let $J$ be finitely generated with the subgroup-field hypotheses, and let $K\lhd J$ satisfy the selective realization property of Definition <a href="#fill:selective-input" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fill:selective-input">11</a>. Every finite family of rational expressions over $\mathbb QJ$ can, after restriction of scalars to a finite-index subgroup $F$, be realized compatibly in the ordinary Novikov rings for both signs of a single real character of $F$.* *In particular, if a finite complex of finitely generated free $\mathbb QJ$-modules is acyclic over $D(J)$, then its restriction is acyclic over both these Novikov rings. If its degree-zero ordinary homology is nonzero, the character is nonzero.
  - Explanation: Selective support realization bridges quotient descent and ordinary Novikov contractions.
- **claim-open-rfrs-novikov-regions** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fill-rfrs-novikov)): Let $J$ be virtually RFRS with the subgroup-field hypotheses. A finite family of bounded complexes of finitely generated free $\mathbb QJ$-modules, with polynomial differential matrices and acyclic extension to $D(J)$, admits simultaneous ordinary Novikov contractions, after passage to a finite-index subgroup $F$, on a nonempty antipodally invariant open subset of $\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}(F,\mathbb R)$. Here the character space has the topology of pointwise convergence. This property can be imposed after any prescribed further finite-index restriction.
  - Explanation: Virtually RFRS groups admit simultaneous contractions on an antipodally invariant open character region.
- **claim-degree-one-bns** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-fill-bns)): Let $J$ be finitely presented, and let $\chi:J\to\mathbb R$ be nonzero. If degree-one homology vanishes over $\widehat{\mathbb QJ}^{\,\chi}$, then $\chi$ belongs to the Bieri–Neumann–Strebel (BNS) invariant. If the vanishing holds for both signs, some nonzero rational character has finitely generated kernel.
  - Explanation: Novikov vanishing gives BNS membership; both signs yield a rational character with finitely generated kernel.
- **claim-dimension-two-free-kernel** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-fill-free-kernel)): Suppose $\mathop{\mathrm{cd}}J\le2$ and $J$ maps onto $\mathbb Z$ with finitely presented kernel $M$. Then $M$ is free.
  - Explanation: A finitely presented cyclic-quotient kernel must be free under the ambient dimension bound.
- **claim-ascending-specialness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-asc-vcs)): Let $F$ be a free group of finite rank and let $\phi:F\to F$ be injective. If $J_\phi$ is word-hyperbolic, then $J_\phi$ is virtually compact special.
  - Explanation: Rank induction and good fillings prove specialness for arbitrary injective ascending input.
- **claim-ascending-field-setup** (theorem, [source](#stmt-asc-field-hypotheses)): An ascending torus of an injective finite-rank free-group endomorphism is torsion-free, locally indicable, coherent, residually finite, and has a finite aspherical complex of dimension at most two. It has the Hughes-free subgroup-field setup used in Theorem <a href="#fill:criterion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fill:criterion">5</a>, and its finite cellular chain complex becomes acyclic over its rational Linnell field.
  - Explanation: Ascending tori provide the finiteness, coherence, and field acyclicity needed by the filling criterion.
- **claim-shift-equivalence** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-asc-shift-equivalence)): Suppose based maps $f:X\to X$ and $g:Y\to Y$ of connected finite graphs admit based maps $q:X\to Y$ and $i:Y\to X$ such that $$qf=gq,\qquad ig=fi,\qquad iq=f^m,\qquad qi=g^m$$ for some $m\ge1$. Their mapping-torus groups are isomorphic, by an isomorphism preserving height.
  - Explanation: Commuting graph factorizations induce height-preserving isomorphisms of mapping-torus groups.
- **claim-relative-tree-model** (classification, [source](#stmt-asc-relative-model)): Let $\phi:F\to F$ be injective and nonsurjective, with $\mathop{\mathrm{rk}}F\ge2$. After replacing $F$ by an iterated image, one of the following holds.* 1. *A finite-index height subgroup of $J_\phi$ is an ascending torus of an injection of a free group of rank strictly smaller than $\mathop{\mathrm{rk}}F$.* 2. *There is a nontrivial free splitting tree $T$ and a $\phi$-equivariant embedding $f:T\to T$ that is a homothety of scale $\lambda\ge1$. The edge-transition matrix is irreducible, every vertex stabilizer is a proper free factor, and the quotient graph is finite.
  - Explanation: After iterated-image replacement, rank reduction or an irreducible tree homothety is available.
- **claim-real-tree-point-stabilizers** (classification, [source](#stmt-asc-point-stabilizers)): The height-zero subgroup of $J_\phi$ has trivial stabilizers of nondegenerate arcs of $\mathcal T$. There are finitely many $J_\phi$-orbits of points with nontrivial height-zero stabilizer. For each such point $x$, the full stabilizer $A_x$ has a finite-index subgroup that is an ascending torus on a proper free factor of $F$. If $\lambda>1$, the family of these point stabilizers is malnormal.
  - Explanation: Nontrivial horizontal point stabilizers form finitely many lower-rank ascending types, malnormal in the expanding case.
- **claim-quasiconvex-ascending-peripherals** (theorem, [source](#stmt-asc-quasiconvex-peripherals)): Each subgroup $A_x$ in Lemma <a href="#asc:point-stabilizers" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="asc:point-stabilizers">23</a> is quasiconvex in $J_\phi$. Consequently the finite malnormal family of these subgroups is a relatively hyperbolic peripheral structure. If the inductive hypothesis holds below rank $\mathop{\mathrm{rk}}F$, every member is hyperbolic and virtually compact special.
  - Explanation: Coarse retractions make the point stabilizers quasiconvex and suitable for rank induction.
- **claim-train-track-good-fillings** (construction, [source](#stmt-asc-good-train-track-filling)): Assume the inductive hypothesis below rank $\mathop{\mathrm{rk}}F$ and use the peripheral family in Lemma <a href="#asc:quasiconvex-peripherals" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="asc:quasiconvex-peripherals">24</a>. For every prescribed finite avoidance set there is a peripheral filling $$\bar J=J_\phi/\langle\!\langle N_x\rangle\!\rangle$$ that is hyperbolic, has finite-by-cyclic peripheral images, and has a finite-index subgroup equal to the mapping-torus group of an expanding train-track map $p:V\to V$ of a finite connected graph. After passing to a height power, the edge-transition components of $p$ are disjoint primitive irreducible blocks with connected invariant supports.
  - Explanation: Avoiding seed folds produces finite graph covers with expanding primitive train-track blocks.
- **claim-injective-train-track-block** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-asc-injective-block)): Let $p:V_0\to V_0$ be a based train-track map of a finite connected graph, fixing its base vertex. Suppose all edges expand, the transition matrix is primitive, and its mapping-torus group is hyperbolic. Then that group is virtually compact special, whether or not $p_*$ is injective.
  - Explanation: Stable image ranks remove fundamental-group noninjectivity before irreducible cubulation.
- **claim-filled-ascending-specialness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-asc-filled-vcs)): The fillings in Lemma <a href="#asc:good-train-track-filling" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="asc:good-train-track-filling">25</a> are virtually compact special.
  - Explanation: Cyclic connector splittings assemble the compact-special train-track blocks.
- **claim-ascending-finite-rank-fibering** (theorem, [source](#stmt-cor-ascending-finite-rank)): Let $F$ be a free group of finite rank and let $\phi:F\to F$ be injective. If $J_\phi$ is word-hyperbolic, it has a finite-index subgroup $H$ fitting into an exact sequence $$1\longrightarrow F_d\longrightarrow H\longrightarrow\mathbb Z \longrightarrow1$$ for some finite $d\geq0$, where $F_d$ is the rank-$d$ free group. Thus $H\cong F_d\rtimes_\alpha\mathbb Z$ for an automorphism $\alpha$ of $F_d$.
  - Explanation: Hyperbolic ascending tori virtually fiber with finite-rank free kernel.
- **claim-actual-row-refinement** (construction, [source](#stmt-row-refinement)): There is an actual graph-of-groups decomposition $$\label{row:three-piece} H=P_-*_{I}Q*_{J}P_+,\qquad I=F(B_0,x),\quad J=F(B_0,y).$$ For nonzero integers $d,n$, its middle group is $$\begin{array}{ll} Q=F(B_0,u),\quad x=u^d,\quad y=u^n, &R=\operatorname{pr}_{p/q}(x,y),\\[1mm] Q=F(B_0,x)*_{\langle z\rangle=\langle u^d\rangle}\langle u\rangle, \quad y=x^{-1}u^n, &R=\operatorname{pr}_{p/q}(xy,z). \end{array}$$ The second group has the same root-extension description with $F(B_0,y)$ as base. Refine the vertices of $T_0$ by this splitting and collapse the original shift edges, whose maps onto their $P$-endpoints are isomorphisms. Denote the resulting tree by $T$.
  - Explanation: Primitive substitution gives explicit injective refinements and permits collapsing the shift edges.
- **claim-row-geometry** (theorem, [source](#stmt-row-geometry)): All coarse and refined rows are hyperbolic, and their incident maps are quasi-isometric embeddings. Refined rows are quasiconvex in their containing coarse row $H$. The coarse Magnus sides satisfy:* 1. *their ordinary intersection is $F(B_0)$, or $F(B_0)*\langle w\rangle$ with $w$ outside the common factor on each side;* 2. *a conjugate intersection can be noncyclic only in the aligned opposite-slot double coset; distinct same-slot cosets intersect at most cyclically;* 3. *the overlap and its shifted copy have full-row-rank Fox matrices in their free sides. They are strongly inert there: for every finitely generated subgroup $U$ of a free side $P$, with overlap $O\le P$, $$\sum_{UgO\in U\backslash P/O} \max\{\mathop{\mathrm{rk}}(U\cap gOg^{-1})-1,0\} \le \max\{\mathop{\mathrm{rk}}U-1,0\}.$$ Proposition <a href="#row:path-inertia" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="row:path-inertia">35</a> proves the simultaneous subgroup-homology injection behind this inequality from the stated matrix property.* *In a nonfree root row $Q$, $z$ is not a proper power in the free base. Distinct cyclic incidences at a free-base vertex of its root splitting consequently have trivial intersection.
  - Explanation: Actual rows have controlled hyperbolic geometry, aligned overlaps, and full-rank Fox matrices.
- **claim-level-homology-basis** (theorem, [source](#stmt-row-level-basis)): Over $D_L$, the two-boundary in <a href="#row:height-presentation" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="row:height-presentation">[row:height-presentation]</a> is injective. Every interval of $k$ consecutive $a$-columns is a basis of $C_1/\mathop{\mathrm{im}}\partial_2$. The corresponding quotient for any refined row, after extension to $D_L$, maps isomorphically to the global quotient. The incident edge-to-row maps are isomorphisms on these quotients, and $$\dim_{D_L}H_1(L;D_L)=k-1.$$
  - Explanation: Extreme-column elimination identifies every actual row quotient with the global level quotient.
- **claim-row-orbit-restriction** (theorem, [source](#stmt-row-restriction)): For $U\leq L$ and an actual level $\mathscr L$, inclusion and the above coefficient transport give an injection $$\label{row:level-restriction} \bigoplus_{\xi\in U\backslash\mathscr L} H_1(U\cap X_\xi;D_U)\ \longrightarrow\ H_1(U;D_U).$$ For $U$ in a vertex row, the analogous sum over one incident slot injects. The same assertions hold for coarse rows. The assertions hold in the induced chain modules before passing to an overfield.
  - Explanation: Induced-module trimming proves simultaneous homology injection for actual level and slot orbits.
- **claim-path-inertia** (bound, [source](#stmt-row-path-inertia)): In $T$ and $T_0$, every path with noncyclic pointwise stabilizer is monotone. For each fixed monotone shape in a fixed absolute level range, the first homologies of its stabilizers, indexed modulo $L$, inject jointly into $H_1(L;D_L)$. A path containing an edge has finitely generated free stabilizer, and a fixed finite shape has finitely many $G$-orbits with nontrivial stabilizer, or finitely many $L$-orbits when its absolute level range is fixed. In particular $$\label{row:rank-budget} \sum_{\gamma\bmod L}\max\{\mathop{\mathrm{rk}}\mathop{\mathrm{Stab}}(\gamma)-1,0\}\leq k-1.$$ The same joint-injection statement holds for continuations of any fixed additional shape inside any subgroup $U$ of a current path stabilizer, with the intersection summands indexed by $U$-orbits. It holds after restriction of the actual induced matrices and double-coset decompositions, not just as a numerical inequality.
  - Explanation: Path stabilizers retain simultaneous homology injections under arbitrary subgroup restriction.
- **claim-cyclic-path-dictionary** (bound, [source](#stmt-row-cyclic-dictionary)): Fix a finite edge-containing path shape. In a reduced tree path fixed pointwise by a nontrivial element, the number of pairwise disjoint subsegments of that shape having cyclic stabilizer is bounded. Monotonicity is not required.
  - Explanation: Repeated oriented cyclic blocks would force an impossible cyclic commensuration by a tree translation.
- **claim-subtree-quasiconvexity-gates** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-row-boundary-gates)): Let a torsion-free hyperbolic group $J$ act cocompactly on a tree of hyperbolic Cayley spaces with uniformly quasi-isometrically embedded edge maps and hyperbolic total space. We use the standard Cayley realization with uniformly proper vertex inclusions and isometric product strips over open edges. For the finite splittings here, properness is uniform: normalize a vertex to the identity and take the maximum intrinsic length of the finitely many elements in each ambient word ball, over the finitely many vertex types. Let $A\leq J$ preserve a connected subtree $Y$, with $A\backslash Y$ finite. Suppose its vertex and edge stabilizers are finitely generated and quasiconvex in the respective rows. Either of the following suffices for $A$ to be quasiconvex in $J$:* 1. *ambient vertex rows are quasiconvex in $J$;* 2. *every edge leaving $Y$ intersects $A$ trivially or cyclically.* *This applies in particular to $G$ acting on $T$ or $T_0$.
  - Explanation: Controlled projections yield ambient quasiconvexity for finite-quotient subtrees with the stated boundary alternatives.
- **claim-finite-row-homology** (classification, [source](#stmt-row-row-finiteness)): Every subgroup $M$ of a refined row with $\beta(M)<\infty$ is finitely generated and quasiconvex in that row. If $\beta(M)=0$, then $M$ is trivial or cyclic.
  - Explanation: Finite field homology forces finite generation and row quasiconvexity.
- **claim-period-rule** (theorem, [source](#stmt-row-period-rule)): Suppose $A\leq G$, $h(A)\neq0$, and $$S=A\cap L,\qquad 0<\beta(S)<\infty.$$ At every actual level $\mathscr L$, inclusion induces an isomorphism $$\bigoplus_{\xi\in S\backslash\mathscr L} H_1(S\cap X_\xi;D_S)\ \longrightarrow\ H_1(S;D_S).$$ Both incident edge-level maps to a vertex level are isomorphisms. Every level sum therefore has dimension $q_X=\beta(S)$. The convex hull $Y$ of the rows with noncyclic $S\cap X_\xi$ contains no edge with trivial $S$-stabilizer. If $A$ is also finitely generated, then $A\backslash Y$ is finite and $A$ is quasiconvex in $G$.
  - Explanation: Height periodicity turns injective level maps into isomorphisms; finite generation then gives ambient quasiconvexity.
- **claim-support-coset-descent** (theorem, [source](#stmt-coeff-support)): The following assertions hold.* 1. *If $S\cap T=\varnothing$, then $\mathcal V(S)\cap\mathcal V(T)=0$.* 2. *There is a $\mathbb Q$-linear map $$\mathcal F\colon D_J\longrightarrow\mathbb Q^J$$ with $\mathcal F(1)=\delta_1$, commuting with every right group translation, such that $v\in\mathcal V(S)$ implies $\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\mathcal F(v)\subseteq S$.* 3. *Let $A,B\le J$ and $C=A\cap B$. If $At\cap Bs$ is empty, then $D_A t\cap D_B s=0$. Otherwise, for any $x\in At\cap Bs$, $$\label{coeff:single-coset} D_A t\cap D_B s=D_Cx.$$ If, in addition, $C$ is separable in both $A$ and $B$, then $$\label{coeff:finite-span} \left(\sum_{g\in J}D_Ag\right) \cap \left(\sum_{g\in J}D_Bg\right) =\sum_{g\in J}D_Cg,$$ where each sum denotes its algebraic, finite-support span.
  - Explanation: Permitted algebraic support gives disjointness, an equivariant scalar map, and intersection descent.
- **claim-hereditary-coefficient-extraction** (theorem, [source](#stmt-coeff-extraction)): Let finitely many normalized rational expressions have hereditary offsets in a finitely generated subgroup $H$, and let $\chi\colon H\twoheadrightarrow\mathbb Z$ be a character with kernel $K$. Expand in the positive skew Laurent field in <a href="#coeff:cyclic-field" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="coeff:cyclic-field">[coeff:cyclic-field]</a>, writing powers of $t$ on the right. Every coefficient has a finite normalized rational expression in $D_K$, with the following properties.* 1. *If a summand is permitted on $S$, the expression for its coefficient of degree $n$ has term patterns contained in $$(S\cap\chi^{-1}(n))t^{-n}.$$ Here $S$ can be replaced by its intersection with $H$.* 2. *Coefficient extraction does not increase the complexity of an arbitrary top expression. If an inverse occurrence is nonhomogeneous, the decrease is strict. In particular, for a normalized operand $P$ whose hereditary offsets are not all killed by $\chi$, every coefficient expression has complexity strictly less than $c(P)$.* 3. *For a collection of top expressions, assume at least one represented top offset equals $1$ and that $\chi$ is nonzero on the subgroup generated by all their hereditary offsets. The joint complexity of the coefficient expressions at each degree is strictly smaller than the original joint complexity.* 4. *If the input is represented in one field coset $D_Aa$, with all inverse operands internal to $A$, a nonzero coefficient of degree $n$ is represented in one coset of $D_{A\cap K}$. Its permitted group coset is $(Aa\cap\chi^{-1}(n))t^{-n}$, and its inverse operands remain internal to $A\cap K$.
  - Explanation: Skew coefficient extraction preserves permitted slices and decreases hereditary complexity in nonhomogeneous cases.
- **claim-rational-series-descent** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-coeff-rational-descent)): Let $E\subseteq F$ be division rings and let conjugation by $u$ induce an automorphism of $F$ preserving $E$. If an element of $F(u)$ has a bounded-below Laurent expansion $$S=\sum_n u^n f_n,\qquad f_n\in E,$$ then $S\in E(u)$.
  - Explanation: A common denominator coordinate over the smaller division ring proves rational descent.
- **claim-semilinear-affiliated-support** (theorem, [source](#stmt-coeff-analytic-support)): Let $G$ be a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group, let $h:G\to\mathbb Z$ be a homomorphism, and put $L=\ker h$. Let $D\le G$ be quasiconvex and put $S=D\cap L$. Choose $g\in G$ and $g_D\in D$ such that $$h(g)=h(g_D)\ne0.$$ Suppose that the division fields in use are embedded in the affiliated group algebras, and that, for an integer $r\ge1$, a row $\lambda\in D_L^{\,1\times r}$ satisfies $$\label{coeff:analytic-semilinear} g\lambda g_D^{-1}=\lambda B,\qquad B\in\operatorname{GL}_r(D_S).$$ Then $$\label{coeff:analytic-support-conclusion} \lambda\in\sum_{xS\in\mathcal P}x\,\mathcal U(S)^{\,1\times r}, \qquad \mathcal P= \{xS:\ x\in L,\ g^m\in xDx^{-1} \text{ for some }m\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}\}.$$ The set $\mathcal P$ is finite. In fact, the same assertion holds for any affiliated row $\lambda$ and any affiliated invertible matrix $B$ satisfying <a href="#coeff:analytic-semilinear" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="coeff:analytic-semilinear">[coeff:analytic-semilinear]</a>.
  - Explanation: Semilinear transport confines affiliated coefficients to finitely many periodic subgroup cosets.
- **claim-affiliated-measure-calculus** (theorem, [source](#stmt-coeff-analytic-calculus)): The affiliated algebra of a finite von Neumann algebra is complete for convergence in measure. Products of tight families are tight. If $a_j\to0$ in measure and $b_j,c_j$ range over tight families, then $b_ja_jc_j\to0$ in measure. These assertions also hold uniformly over an additional index.* *Positive square roots are continuous in measure on positive affiliated operators, and inversion is continuous in measure on positive affiliated units. A uniformly norm-bounded family that tends to zero in measure tends to zero in $L^1(\tau)$; the same assertion holds uniformly.
  - Explanation: Measure completeness and tightness estimates justify products, functional calculus, and bounded trace convergence.
- **claim-spectral-projection-comparison** (bound, [source](#stmt-coeff-analytic-projection)): Let $T,X$ be positive affiliated units in $\mathcal M$, and let $t>0$. For $p_+=1_{(t,\infty)}(T)$ and $p_-=1_{(0,t)}(T)$, $$\begin{aligned} \tau\bigl(p_+F(T,X)\bigr) &\ge \tau\bigl(p_+F(t1,X)\bigr), \label{coeff:analytic-high}\\ \tau\bigl(p_-F(T,X)\bigr) &\le \tau\bigl(p_-F(t1,X)\bigr). \label{coeff:analytic-low} \end{aligned}$$
  - Explanation: Schur-complement monotonicity gives high and low spectral trace comparisons.
- **claim-affiliated-positive-mean** (theorem, [source](#stmt-coeff-analytic-mean)): Let $X_n$, $n\in\mathbb Z$, be positive affiliated units in a finite von Neumann algebra. Suppose that both $\{X_n\}$ and $\{X_n^{-1}\}$ are tight. There is a unique positive affiliated unit $P$ satisfying $$\label{coeff:analytic-mean-equation} \mathfrak M_nF(P,X_n)=\tfrac12\,1.$$ The construction is covariant under congruence by affiliated invertible operators, including affiliated invertible maps between corners with their restricted traces.
  - Explanation: Clipping, uniform spectral tails, and measure comparison construct a unique covariant affiliated mean.
- **claim-bounded-core-comparisons** (theorem, [source](#stmt-gate-comparisons)): Assume the expansion package. For a fixed bounded pair of positions $i,j$, let $K$ stabilize the segment spanned by $W_i\cup W_j$. There are $K$-equivariant coarse quasi-isometries between the $K$-cores in $R_i,R_j$. They have coarse inverses, preserve the line endspaces of every further window, and are coarsely compatible on every fixed finite diagram of positions. The constants depend on the bounded diagram, not on a further window carrying the arc.
  - Explanation: Finite relative core quotients supply compatible equivariant comparisons on bounded diagrams.
- **claim-carried-arc-flaring** (bound, [source](#stmt-gate-flaring)): Under the expansion package there are integers $b,R>0$ with the following property. An arc of length at least $R$ carried across the positions $[-b,b]$ has trimmed image of length at least $100$ times its original length in one of the comparisons $0\to-b$ and $0\to b$.
  - Explanation: A corridor estimate forces sufficiently long carried arcs to expand in one direction.
- **claim-cyclic-index-control** (bound, [source](#stmt-gate-cyclic-indices)): Assume the expansion package. Fix a bounded sampling step, and let $W_j$ be the successive short windows, with sampled edges $e_j$, along an interval of a monotone trajectory. The interval may be finite, one-sided infinite, or bilateral. Put $$H_j=\mathop{\mathrm{Stab}}(W_j),\qquad K_j=\mathop{\mathrm{Stab}}\bigl(\operatorname{Hull}(W_j\cup W_{j+1})\bigr).$$ Let $C=\langle c_0\rangle\le L$ be a maximal cyclic subgroup of $G$. Suppose $C\cap K_j$ is nontrivial and loxodromic in the short-window trees for every adjacent pair. Write $$C\cap H_j=\langle c_0^{q_j}\rangle,\qquad C\cap K_j=\langle c_0^{m_j}\rangle, \qquad q_j,m_j>0.$$ There are uniform constants $B,E$ such that both indices $m_j/q_j$ and $m_j/q_{j+1}$ are at most $B$, and at most $E$ of these indices differ from one over the whole interval. In particular all partial products of their ratios lie between $B^{-E}$ and $B^E$. For an infinite interval some nonidentity element of $C$ belongs to every $K_j$.
  - Explanation: Marked continuation pairs bound cyclic index changes and give a common surviving power.
- **claim-rational-line-persistence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-gate-rational-persistence)): Suppose a bilateral trajectory carries, in $R_0$, the whole axis of a loxodromic element $c\in H_0$ through every finite subwindow containing position zero. Some nonzero power of $c$ fixes the entire trajectory pointwise.
  - Explanation: Cyclic index control upgrades window-dependent powers to one common translation.
- **claim-phase-uniqueness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-gate-phase-uniqueness)): There is a uniform depth $N$ such that two trajectories carrying the same expanding event of length $2R$, and agreeing through depth $N$ in its expanding direction including the short comparison windows, cannot subsequently diverge in that direction while still carrying the arc. One or both trajectories may be finite. The same conclusion holds for arcs carried by all finite subwindows of an infinite trajectory.
  - Explanation: Exponential flaring exceeds all bounded cyclic pullback losses before a late divergence.
- **claim-sampling-offset-persistence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-gate-offset)): For an ordinary bilateral trajectory, an expanding event of a given sign produces events of that sign at every sufficiently distant row in that direction, not merely on its stride-$b$ subsequence.
  - Explanation: Bounded-offset comparisons prevent opposite persistent expansion on different sampling subsequences.
- **claim-decreasing-free-cores** (theorem, [source](#stmt-gate-decreasing-cores)): Let $K_n$ be a decreasing sequence of finitely generated subgroups of one free row, with uniformly bounded ranks, and put $M=\bigcap_n K_n$. Then $M$ is a finite-rank free group. Its core graph embeds in that of $K_n$ for all sufficiently large $n$, and its first field homology injects there.
  - Explanation: Finite identification tests embed the intersection core at sufficiently late stages.
- **claim-branching-tail-groups** (classification, [source](#stmt-gate-tail-groups)): There are finitely many orbits of branching bilateral trajectories and of branching one-sided tails. Every branching bilateral trajectory is periodic under a nonzero-height element; every branching one-sided tail is eventually periodic.* *For a monotone ray from an edge $e$ to an end $z$, let $$M_{z,e}=\mathop{\mathrm{Stab}}([e,z))$$ be its pointwise stabilizer. This is a finite-rank free group. Its homology injects in sufficiently long finite-prefix homologies, and the finite-path restriction rule also holds on restricting within a later tail group, with the same common-level and orbit conventions. If some $M_{z,e}$ is noncyclic, let $Y_z$ be the union of all monotone rays to $z$ having noncyclic stabilizer, and let $D_z=\mathop{\mathrm{Stab}}_G(z)$. Then:* 1. *$Y_z$ is connected, $D_z$ has a height translator with axis in $Y_z$, and tail ranks along such an axis are constant;* 2. *$D_z\cap L$ is transitive on the $Y_z$-edges of each fixed level;* 3. *$D_z$ is quasiconvex in $G$ and virtually an ascending mapping torus of a finite-rank free group; in particular it is virtually compact special.
  - Explanation: Finite branching states yield periodic tails, level transitivity, and compact-special end groups.
- **claim-periodic-switches** (classification, [source](#stmt-gate-switches)): Every switch trajectory is periodic. For an active color $z$ occurring at an edge $e$, the tail group $M_{z,e}$ is noncyclic. There are finitely many orbits of active colors and of switch trajectories. A switch trajectory has both signs at every row.
  - Explanation: Switches are periodic, and every active tail group is noncyclic.
- **claim-local-switch-tree** (theorem, [source](#stmt-gate-local-switch-tree)): There is a uniform depth such that the following holds for every centered monotone window $W$ whose two endpoints are at least that far from its sampling center and whose pointwise stabilizer is noncyclic. The colors realized in the central core of $\mathop{\mathrm{Stab}}(W)$ are exactly the active ends $z$ with $W\subset Y_z$. These vertices, together with the switch trajectories traversing $W$, form a nonempty connected tree, denoted $\mathcal C(W)$. If it is an isolated vertex locally, that vertex is isolated in $\mathcal C$.
  - Explanation: Deep window cores record exactly a connected tree of active ends and switches.
- **claim-mark-coarsening-orbits** (theorem, [source](#stmt-gate-mark-orbits)): The components of each $\mathcal C_{j,l}$ form one $S$-orbit. Their quotient vertex, edge, and incidence counts are finite and do not change as $j$ increases and $l$ decreases, including after the two levels cross. The corresponding vertex and edge ranks do not change either.
  - Explanation: Period translations preserve quotient incidence data and subgroup ranks through mark coarsening.
- **claim-simultaneous-incident-free-factors** (theorem, [source](#stmt-gate-incident-factors)): At every vertex of every split action, the nontrivial incident edge groups, indexed by incidence-orbit representatives, are simultaneous free factors of its vertex group, up to separately chosen inner conjugations.
  - Explanation: Disjoint embedded switch cores and Kurosh decomposition give simultaneous incident free factors.
- **claim-proper-free-quotient-obstruction** (bound, [source](#stmt-gate-free-quotient)): Let $F_r$ map onto a nontrivial subgroup $B\le L$, and use $D_L$ coefficients. If this map has nontrivial kernel, then $$\dim_{D_L}H_1(B;D_L)\le r-2.$$ In particular, it cannot surject onto a group containing a subgroup whose ambient homology image has dimension $r-1$.
  - Explanation: A shortest kernel relation contributes a nonzero Fox boundary and lowers field homology.
- **claim-switch-component-trees** (theorem, [source](#stmt-gate-component-tree)): Every component of the actual switch graph is a tree. For a nonisolated component with stabilizer $A$ and $S=A\cap L$, there is an integer $r\ge2$ such that $S$ is a nested union of rank-$r$ free groups and $$\dim_{D_L}H_1(S;D_L)=r-1.$$ These approximants and $S$ have injective ambient first-homology maps. Moreover $A$ is finitely generated, quasiconvex, virtually compact special, and field-acyclic.
  - Explanation: Homological rigidity rules out component circuits and controls the full component stabilizer.
- **claim-periodic-path-capture** (construction, [source](#stmt-gate-capture)): Unless $G$ is already virtually compact special by the acylindrical case, there is an invariant system of actual objects, finite modulo $G$, with full stabilizers $A$ and kernels $S=A\cap L$, having these properties:* 1. *$h(A)\ne0$; each $A$ is quasiconvex, virtually compact special, and field-acyclic.* 2. *Each $S$ is a nested union of finite-rank free approximants of one constant rank at least two. Its field first-homology dimension is positive and finite, and its ambient homology detects every noncyclic subgroup.* 3. *For representatives of the actual object orbits under $L$, the maps $$\bigoplus H_1(S;D_L)\longrightarrow H_1(L;D_L)$$ are jointly injective. Distinct actual object stabilizers intersect in at most cyclic groups.* 4. *There is a uniform length such that the pointwise stabilizer of every longer noncyclically stabilized actual path, in $T_0$ or in the refined tree $T$, is wholly contained in one of these kernels $S$.
  - Explanation: Periodic component groups capture whole long noncyclic path stabilizers with jointly injective homology.
- **claim-cyclic-incidence-forest** (theorem, [source](#stmt-close-join-forest)): The cyclic incidence graph has finitely many $G$-orbits of edges and is a forest.
  - Explanation: Support-controlled Fox fillings exclude circuits in the cyclic incidence graph.
- **claim-cyclic-component-groups** (theorem, [source](#stmt-close-join-components)): Let $A'$ be the full stabilizer of a component of the cyclic incidence forest, and put $S'=A'\cap L$. Then $A'$ is finitely generated, quasiconvex in $G$, virtually compact special, and field-acyclic; $h(A')\ne0$ and $0<\beta(S')<\infty$. Stabilizers of different new components intersect at most cyclically. If $e_+$ and $c_+$ count, modulo $S'$, the incidences and cyclic vertices with nonzero height image, respectively, then $$\label{close:join-dimension} \beta(S')=\sum_{v\in S'\backslash\mathrm{Old}} \beta(S_v)+e_+-c_+.$$ Here the old vertex groups are understood in their actual conjugate positions. No joint ambient injection for the new system is assumed in this lemma.
  - Explanation: Cyclic joins preserve geometric and field properties before joint ambient injection is proved.
- **claim-cyclic-join-detection** (theorem, [source](#stmt-close-join-detection)): Every noncyclic subgroup of a new height kernel $S'$ is detected in $H_1(S';D_{S'})$. Its image will therefore be detected in ambient homology once the joint injection below is established.
  - Explanation: Normalized path differences detect noncyclic subgroups in the newly joined kernel.
- **claim-cyclic-join-injection** (theorem, [source](#stmt-close-join-injection)): For the new component system the map $$\bigoplus_{i\in L\backslash\mathcal D'}H_1(S'_i;D_L) \longrightarrow H_1(L;D_L)$$ is injective. Consequently a cyclic-join round preserves admissibility and does not decrease the budget. A round containing a positive-height cyclic join increases the budget by at least one.
  - Explanation: Semilinear support localization preserves joint injection and increases the budget at positive-height joins.
- **claim-finite-strict-closure** (construction, [source](#stmt-close-strict-system)): Iterating cyclic joins stops after finitely many rounds. The final system is admissible and strictly malnormal: stabilizers of distinct objects have trivial intersection. Each is the full stabilizer of its object. For each final object $d$, the union of all actual rows $x$ with $X_x\cap S_d\ne1$ is a connected subtree $Z_d$ with finite $D_d$-quotient, where $D_d$ is its object stabilizer and $S_d=D_d\cap L$.
  - Explanation: Budget growth and finite generation of horizontal unions make cyclic closure terminate.
- **claim-root-closed-object-subtrees** (theorem, [source](#stmt-close-strict-subtrees)): In a strict system, each $D_d$ is root-closed in $G$. Its subtree $Z_d$ consists exactly of the actual rows with $M_x^d=X_x\cap S_d\ne1$, and has finite $D_d$-quotient. At every actual level the sum of the homologies of the $M_x^d$, over $S_d$-orbits, maps isomorphically onto $H_1(S_d)$. At an actual vertex the analogous sum over one slot maps isomorphically onto $H_1(M_x^d)$.
  - Explanation: Strictness gives root closure and complete level and slot homology identities.
- **claim-raw-horizontal-jumps** (construction, [source](#stmt-close-raw-jumps)): Fix an actual row group $X$ at a given level, and represent its actual rows by frame cosets $pX\subset L$. A jump from $pX$ to $qX$ through one object $d$ has a raw horizontal one-chain representative with divergence $q-p$. Its coefficient support is contained both in a finite union of $S_dr$ and in the union of the actual $X$-cosets incident to $d$. Root-row representatives are taken before eliminating the root relation.
  - Explanation: Period isomorphisms produce support-controlled jump chains with the required divergence.
- **claim-root-cylinder-correction** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-close-root-cylinder)): Suppose the actual row is $$X=B*_{\langle z\rangle=\langle u^a\rangle}\langle u\rangle, \qquad a>1,$$ where $B$ is free and $z$ is root-indivisible in $B$. Put $U=\langle u\rangle$, $\alpha=1+u+\cdots+u^{a-1}$, and $R=\alpha\mathbf e_u-d_B(z)$. Let $V=\sum_iV_i$ be a finite sum of raw vectors whose coefficients have the support patterns of Lemma <a href="#close:raw-jumps" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="close:raw-jumps">70</a>, for distinct members of a strict quasiconvex system. If $V=PR$ in the division-field chain module (necessarily $P=V_u\alpha^{-1}$), then, after applying the simultaneous scalar-function map, $P$ is supported within a bounded neighborhood of the corresponding finite union of peripheral neighborhoods. It can be split among those neighborhoods outside a bounded set, so that subtracting the corresponding multiples of $R$ makes each $V_i$ finitely supported without changing its divergence. The same assertion holds after restriction to a specified actual $X$-coset.
  - Explanation: Isolated root-cylinder equations permit finite-support corrections without changing divergence.
- **claim-folded-row-incidence-tree** (theorem, [source](#stmt-close-folded-row)): For every folded place $w$, its incidence graph $\Gamma_w$ is a tree. The $Y_w$-action is cocompact, with one orbit of actual row vertices; its vertex groups are the indicated $X_x$ and $S_d$, and its incidence groups are $M_x^d$. The inclusion induces an isomorphism $$H_1(Y_w;D_L)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }H_1(L;D_L).$$
  - Explanation: Divergence obstructions exclude horizontal incidence circuits and identify folded-row homology.
- **claim-folded-level-detection** (theorem, [source](#stmt-close-folded-separation)): Every noncyclic subgroup of $Y_w$ is detected in ambient height-kernel homology. Stabilizers of two distinct folded places at the same level intersect at most cyclically.
  - Explanation: Normalized path detection separates distinct folded places at the same level.
- **claim-folded-slot-restriction** (theorem, [source](#stmt-close-folded-slot)): Fix a folded vertex $v$ and one slot of incident folded edges $f$. Let $K_f$ be the image of the endpoint map $\Gamma_f\to\Gamma_v$. Then $K_f$ is a $Y_f$-cocompact subtree, every object vertex $d$ of $\Gamma_v$ occurs in exactly one such $K_f$ with its full stabilizer, and any absent incidence has at most cyclic stabilizer. For each $H\le Y_v$ the natural map $$\label{close:slot-injection} \bigoplus_{f\bmod H}H_1(H\cap Y_f;D_L) \longrightarrow H_1(H;D_L)$$ is injective.
  - Explanation: Actual slot restrictions survive folding, including both root alternatives.
- **claim-strict-folded-tree** (construction, [source](#stmt-close-folding)): The quotient $\widehat T$ is a tree with one $L$-orbit at each level, and every $Z_d$ maps onto a monotone line $\ell_d$. Its row groups and slot maps have the conclusions of Lemmas <a href="#close:folded-row" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="close:folded-row">72</a> and <a href="#close:folded-separation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="close:folded-separation">73</a> and Proposition <a href="#close:folded-slot" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="close:folded-slot">74</a>. Stabilizers of finite monotone paths in any fixed height range inject jointly on first field homology into $L$, over path-orbit representatives.
  - Explanation: Strict folding preserves the tree, level orbits, object lines, and joint path homology.
- **claim-shared-end-stabilizers** (theorem, [source](#stmt-close-end-kernels)): Suppose two distinct folded lines share an end. Choose the positive orientation if possible, reversing all orientations otherwise. The set of distinct positive ends $\xi$ of the $\ell_d$ has finitely many $G$-orbits. For $A_\xi=\mathop{\mathrm{Stab}}_G(\xi)$ and $S_\xi=A_\xi\cap L$, one has $h(A_\xi)\ne0$, and $S_\xi$ is the increasing union of pointwise tail stabilizers on any chosen line ending at $\xi$. Distinct $A_\xi$ intersect at most cyclically.
  - Explanation: End kernels are increasing tail unions, and distinct end groups intersect at most cyclically.
- **claim-joint-tail-homology** (theorem, [source](#stmt-close-tail-injection)): For representatives of the $L$-orbits of positive ends, the map $$\bigoplus_\xi H_1(S_\xi;D_L)\longrightarrow H_1(L;D_L)$$ is injective. The homology of every pointwise tail group $K$ also injects into ambient homology and has finite dimension. In particular $0<\beta(S_\xi)<\infty$.
  - Explanation: Finite tests of decreasing prefix groups give tail injection; end kernels have positive finite homology.
- **claim-tail-free-product** (theorem, [source](#stmt-close-tail-splitting)): Let $K$ be the pointwise stabilizer of a positive ray contained in an old line, starting at an actual free-edge level $w$. An object vertex of $\Gamma_w$ is called full if its line contains that entire tail. There are finitely many $K$-orbits of full vertices. With representatives $d_1,\ldots,d_m$, one has $$\label{close:tail-product} K\cong\Bigl(*_{j=1}^m S_{d_j}\Bigr)*F_r, \qquad r<\infty.$$ The displayed embeddings of full factors are their actual subgroup embeddings, up to the usual independent choices of conjugating basepoint paths.
  - Explanation: Simultaneous boundary factors split a tail group into its actual full kernels and a finite-rank free factor.
- **claim-virtually-free-stable-image** (theorem, [source](#stmt-close-virtually-free-endo)): Let $V$ be a finitely generated virtually free group and $\phi:V\to V$ an endomorphism. The sequence $\ker\phi^n$ is eventually stationary. Its ascending torus is therefore isomorphic to the ascending torus of an injective endomorphism of a finitely generated virtually free group. In the injective case this torus has a finite-index subgroup that is an ascending torus of an injection of a finite-rank free group.
  - Explanation: Stable image ranks reduce virtually free presentation tori to injective free ascending tori.
- **claim-end-specialness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-close-end-vcs)): Each end stabilizer $A_\xi$ is finitely generated, quasiconvex in $G$, field-acyclic, and virtually compact special. It is torsion-free, locally indicable, coherent, of type $F$, and of cohomological dimension at most two.
  - Explanation: Tail decompositions, virtually free fillings, and the filling criterion establish compact-special end groups.
- **claim-shared-end-budget-growth** (theorem, [source](#stmt-close-end-growth)): Replacing the objects by distinct end stabilizers preserves all admissibility conditions. If some two distinct old lines share an end in the chosen orientation, this replacement strictly increases the budget. Subsequent cyclic closure does not decrease it.
  - Explanation: A genuine shared-end replacement strictly increases the injected homology budget.
- **claim-terminal-periodic-system** (construction, [source](#stmt-close-terminal-system)): Starting with the system of Proposition <a href="#gate:capture" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="gate:capture">62</a>, finitely many cyclic-closure and end-enlargement rounds produce an admissible strict malnormal quasiconvex virtually compact special system $\{D_d\}$, with $S_d=D_d\cap L$, and a folded tree $\widehat T$ having all the conclusions of Corollary <a href="#close:folding" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="close:folding">75</a>. The associated monotone lines $\ell_d$ of distinct objects share no end. Actual long noncyclic path stabilizers remain captured, the kernels still detect all noncyclic subgroups, and their joint homology budget is at most $k-1$.
  - Explanation: Finite closure and enlargement rounds produce malnormal peripherals whose folded lines share no end.
- **claim-fixed-ray-capture** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-transfer-ray-capture)): If $1\ne c\in L$ fixes a monotone ray of $\widehat T$ pointwise, then its end is an end of exactly one object line $\ell_d$, and $c\in S_d$.
  - Explanation: A nontrivial horizontal ray fixer belongs to the unique object kernel at that end.
- **claim-bounded-peripheral-incidences** (bound, [source](#stmt-transfer-bounded-incidence)): There is a uniform constant $C$ such that $Y_w\cap S_d\ne1$ implies $d_{\widehat T}(w,\ell_d)\le C$. There are finitely many orbits of these incidences. If $w\notin\ell_d$, the intersection is cyclic.
  - Explanation: Off-line peripheral intersections are cyclic and occur within bounded distance and finitely many orbit types.
- **claim-relative-row-geometry** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-transfer-relative-rows)): Under the local hypotheses just listed, each folded vertex row $Y_v$ is hyperbolic relative to its finite induced peripheral system, and each adjacent edge map $Y_f\hookrightarrow Y_v$ is an exact relative embedding. The assertions remain valid after adjoining the external maximal cyclic intersections, provided their incidence lists satisfy the same local hypotheses.
  - Explanation: Incidence-tree gluings give relative hyperbolicity and exact adjacent embeddings.
- **claim-partial-metric-hyperbolicity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-transfer-partial-hyperbolicity)): The tree of relative row spaces before filling is hyperbolic. Its metric is quasi-isometric to the partial Cayley metric on $G$ obtained by allowing arbitrary $S_d$-moves and, if present, arbitrary moves in the additional root cyclics.
  - Explanation: Relative fillings of peripheral clusters give a hyperbolic partial metric before quotienting.
- **claim-unfilled-path-comparison** (theorem, [source](#stmt-transfer-unfilled-comparison)): Fix two exact relative embeddings into a row, and fixed ordinary endpoint connectors. Expanded intrinsic geodesics have the following comparison. Large-angle apices occur on both paths in the same order. Their corresponding inbound and outbound germs differ by peripheral elements from fixed finite lists. Between successive marked apices there are paired ordinary subgroup-frame checkpoints, at bounded successive path steps, whose discrepancies lie in a fixed finite subset of the row. The same conclusion holds in the central part of long paths tending to the endpoints of a common loxodromic element, with constants independent of remote endpoint costs.
  - Explanation: Ordered apex matching and proper angles give finite original frame discrepancies.
- **claim-unfilled-exact-intersections** (theorem, [source](#stmt-transfer-intersection)): If $B,C$ have exact relative embeddings into a row $J$, then for every fixed $g\in J$, the subgroup $E=B\cap gCg^{-1}$ is relatively hyperbolic and has exact relative embeddings into $J$, $B$, and $gCg^{-1}$.
  - Explanation: Checkpoint orbits relatively generate intersections and preserve exact peripheral embeddings.
- **claim-unfilled-double-coset-finiteness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-transfer-unfilled-double-cosets)): For fixed exact relative embeddings of $B,C$ in a row $J$, the double cosets $BgC$ having nonparabolic intersection $B\cap gCg^{-1}$ have representatives in a fixed finite subset of $J$.
  - Explanation: Central comparison of common loxodromic endpoints bounds nonparabolic double-coset representatives.
- **claim-relative-window-factors** (theorem, [source](#stmt-transfer-window-splitting)): For a sufficiently long monotone folded path $W$, its pointwise stabilizer $H$ has a finite relative free-product decomposition $$H=\Bigl(*_{j=1}^m(H\cap S_{d_j})\Bigr)*F_r.$$ The factors represent exactly the nontrivial peripheral intersections, up to $H$-conjugacy. Vertices of the corresponding relative Bass–Serre tree that have nontrivial stabilizer carry injective, equivariant labels by actual objects $d$. The trivial vertices can be chosen of finite valence.
  - Explanation: Long windows split over all actual peripheral intersections with injective object labels.
- **claim-terminal-path-bound** (bound, [source](#stmt-transfer-terminal-paths)): There is a length $n_0$ such that every segment of $\widehat T$ of length at least $n_0$ has trivial, cyclic, or parabolic pointwise stabilizer. Moreover there is a uniform bound on the length of a segment fixed by any nontrivial height-zero element lying outside all the $S_d$.
  - Explanation: Expansion and the absence of shared object ends bound nonparabolic segment stabilization.
- **claim-additional-root-peripheral** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-transfer-root-cyclic)): In the root case in which no power of the root cyclic group is claimed by the object system, its maximal cyclic overgroup may be added to the peripheral family. Its nontrivial incidences have finite orbit lists, and the relative embeddings and finite-path conclusions continue to hold with the enlarged induced systems.
  - Explanation: An unclaimed root cyclic can be peripheralized while preserving finite incidence and embedding properties.
- **claim-induced-subgroup-fillings** (theorem, [source](#stmt-transfer-subgroup-filling)): For a fixed finite collection of exact relative embeddings into rows, one can choose the finite tests in Definition <a href="#transfer:finite-tests" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="transfer:finite-tests">94</a> so that every sufficiently long filling satisfying them has the following properties. Each standalone induced subgroup filling injects into the row filling, and the resulting coned embeddings have common quasi-isometry constants independent of the filling. Their expanded intrinsic geodesics have no repeated ambient peripheral apex.
  - Explanation: Finite membership tests ensure standalone subgroup injection and uniform relative geometry after filling.
- **claim-filled-path-comparison** (theorem, [source](#stmt-transfer-path-comparison)): For the fixed embeddings and connectors of Lemma <a href="#transfer:unfilled-comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="transfer:unfilled-comparison">88</a>, every sufficiently long filling satisfying Lemma <a href="#transfer:subgroup-filling" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="transfer:subgroup-filling">95</a> has the same comparison conclusions. All discrepancy and peripheral-germ lists are images of fixed finite lists in the original groups, independent of the filling.
  - Explanation: Uniform relative filling constants preserve the original finite comparison dictionaries.
- **claim-filled-double-coset-finiteness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-transfer-double-cosets)): For fixed original exact relative embeddings of $B,C$ in a row, every double coset in a sufficiently long filling whose intersection contains an infinite-order loxodromic element has a representative in the image of a fixed finite original list. The list is independent of the double coset and of the filling.
  - Explanation: Common loxodromic endpoints yield representatives from a filling-independent original list.
- **claim-exact-intersection-transfer** (theorem, [source](#stmt-transfer-exact-intersection)): Fix exact relative embeddings $B,C\hookrightarrow J$ with the full-or-cyclic induced peripheral systems described above, and fix $g\in J$. There are finitely many compatibility requests of Definition <a href="#transfer:finite-tests" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="transfer:finite-tests">94</a>, determined in the original groups, such that every sufficiently long filling satisfying them has $$\bar B\cap\bar g\bar C\bar g^{-1} =\overline{B\cap gCg^{-1}}.$$ The notation $\bar B$, $\bar C$ denotes the embedded standalone fillings given by Lemma <a href="#transfer:subgroup-filling" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="transfer:subgroup-filling">95</a>.
  - Explanation: Consistent connector lifts and peripheral product tests prevent new quotient intersections.
- **claim-finite-path-filling-transfer** (theorem, [source](#stmt-transfer-finite-path-transfer)): Fix an integer $n$. Under the terminal row hypotheses, there is a finite set of original compatibility requests such that every sufficiently long compatible filling has the following properties.* 1. *The induced row fillings and edge fillings form the quotient graph of groups for $\bar G$.* 2. *Every reduced path of length at most $n$ downstairs with infinite stabilizer lifts, after the permitted changes of Bass–Serre representatives, to an actual reduced path upstairs. Its stabilizer is exactly the image of the actual path stabilizer.* 3. *Taking $n$ at least the terminal path bound, the resulting Bass–Serre action is acylindrical: sufficiently long segment stabilizers are finite of uniformly bounded order. Each filled row is hyperbolic and each edge map is quasi-isometric.* *Here the ambient filled group is hyperbolic by sufficiently long filling of the original relatively hyperbolic pair: the periodic peripheral reductions are finite-by-cyclic and hence hyperbolic, and the additional cyclic reductions are finite. The conclusion about ambient quasiconvexity is proved separately below.
  - Explanation: Finite recursive compatibility requests transfer path stabilizers exactly and yield acylindrical filled splittings.
- **claim-quasiconvex-coset-projections** (theorem, [source](#stmt-transfer-coset-projection)): Fix finitely many quasiconvex subgroup types in a hyperbolic group $J$, with its ordinary Cayley metric. There are uniform constants $R,C$ with the following property. For types $H,K$ and a coset $gK$, either the projection of $H$ to $gK$ has diameter at most $C$, or there are $h\in H,k\in K$ such that $$w=h^{-1}gk,\qquad \|w\|\le R.$$ After translation by $h^{-1}$, that projection lies within distance $C$ of $(H\cap wKw^{-1})w$. Thus the unbounded alternative involves only finitely many normalized intersection types. These intersections are quasiconvex in the row and in the corresponding attaching group.
  - Explanation: Projection is bounded or controlled by a finite normalized intersection type.
- **claim-acylindrical-ambient-quasiconvexity** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-transfer-ambient-qc)): Let $A$ be a hyperbolic group expressed as a finite graph of finitely generated hyperbolic groups. Suppose the edge maps are quasi-isometric embeddings and there is an integer $n$ such that every length-$n$ Bass–Serre segment has finite pointwise stabilizer. Then every vertex and edge group is quasiconvex in $A$. In particular this applies to the filled graph of groups of Theorem <a href="#transfer:finite-path-transfer" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="transfer:finite-path-transfer">99</a>.
  - Explanation: Finite-depth normalized projections give coarse retractions onto vertex rows.
- **claim-local-incidence-cones** (theorem, [source](#stmt-kernel-local-cones)): For a vertex $x\in Z_D$ and either slot, the incidence chain map $$\bigoplus_{\substack{e\text{ in the slot at }x\\ \bmod M_x}} \mathbb QD\otimes_{\mathbb QM_e}C_*(M_e) \longrightarrow \mathbb QD\otimes_{\mathbb QM_x}C_*(M_x)$$ has a finite based free mapping cone over $\mathbb QD$ which becomes contractible over $D_D$. There are finitely many such cones up to $D$.
  - Explanation: Local period isomorphisms make the finite induced incidence cones field-contractible.
- **claim-restricted-novikov-openness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-kernel-novikov-open)): There is a normal finite-index subgroup $H_0\unlhd D$ and a nonempty open cone $$\mathcal O_0\subset\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}(H_0,\mathbb R)$$ on which all the restricted local cones admit contractions over the ordinary rational group Novikov ring. This property persists after passing to any further finite-index subgroup, with a possibly new nonempty open cone.
  - Explanation: Virtual RFRS contractions persist on open cones after further finite-index restrictions.
- **claim-visible-independent-evaluations** (construction, [source](#stmt-kernel-visibility)): After a further normal finite-index refinement of $H_0$, the following conditions hold, and persist under further finite-index refinement. For each required nontrivial group $M$, there is $u_M\in M\cap H_0$ on which some rational character of $H_0$ is nonzero. For every specified pair $\langle a\rangle,\langle b\rangle$ with trivial intersection, evaluation on positive powers of $a,b$ in $H_0$ defines a surjection $$\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}(H_0,\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow\mathbb Q^2.$$ The conditions hold for all the conjugated tests as well.
  - Explanation: Virtual cyclic and free retractions supply nonvanishing and independent character evaluations.
- **claim-finite-cyclic-separation** (construction, [source](#stmt-kernel-cyclic-separation)): There is a normal finite-index subgroup $H\unlhd D$, contained in the prescribed $H_0$, such that every specified pair $\langle a\rangle,\langle b\rangle$ has nontrivial images with trivial intersection in $D/H$. Every specified generator may additionally be required to have order divisible by a prescribed integer, and larger than a prescribed bound.
  - Explanation: Deep cyclic quotients and residual finiteness preserve specified orders and disjoint cyclic images.
- **claim-generic-integral-characters** (construction, [source](#stmt-kernel-characters)): There is a nonempty finite family of integral characters $\chi_j:H\to\mathbb Z$, each giving all the local Novikov contractions, such that:* 1. *every $\chi_j$ is nonzero on each required $M^0$ and on the required power in $H$ of every specified cyclic generator;* 2. *for each specified pair $a,b$, if $m_a,m_b$ are their orders modulo $H$, then $$\bigl(\chi_j(a^{m_a})\bigr)_j,\qquad \bigl(\chi_j(b^{m_b})\bigr)_j$$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb Q$;* 3. *the family is closed under conjugation by $D$.* *There are arbitrarily large odd primes $\ell$ for which all these nonzero evaluations remain nonzero and all these pairs remain independent modulo $\ell$.
  - Explanation: Generic integral tuples and conjugation closure preserve local contractions and independent cyclic evaluations.
- **claim-finite-field-specialization** (construction, [source](#stmt-kernel-scalar-specialization)): One can choose such an odd prime $\ell$, followed by a finite field $\mathbb k$ of arbitrarily large characteristic different from $\ell$, containing all $\ell$-th roots of unity, so that for every $j$ and every $\lambda^\ell=1$, $\lambda\ne1$, the local restriction maps $$H^1(M_x^0;\mathbb k_{\lambda^{\chi_j}}) \longrightarrow \bigoplus_{\substack{e\text{ in the chosen slot at }x\\ \bmod M_x^0}} H^1(M_e^0;\mathbb k_{\lambda^{\chi_j}})$$ are isomorphisms. Actual attaching conjugations are included in this notation. All these local groups have zero $H^0$ for these coefficients.
  - Explanation: Rational contraction denominators can be avoided at all required nontrivial cyclic modes.
- **claim-actual-level-cohomology** (theorem, [source](#stmt-kernel-level-cohomology)): For every $j,\lambda$ as in Lemma <a href="#kernel:scalar-specialization" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="kernel:scalar-specialization">107</a>, and every vertex or edge level $r$ of $Z_D$, restriction is an isomorphism $$H^1(S_0;\mathbb k_{\lambda^{\chi_j}}) \longrightarrow \prod_{\substack{\xi\text{ at level }r\\\bmod S_0}} H^1(M_\xi^0;\mathbb k_{\lambda^{\chi_j}}). \tag{K1}\label{kernel:level-equation}$$ The product on the right is finite. In particular the group on the left is finite-dimensional, and restriction to any individual actual stabilizer is onto.
  - Explanation: Local restriction isomorphisms propagate all cohomology data uniquely along the height line.
- **claim-exact-local-annihilators** (construction, [source](#stmt-kernel-exact-kernel)): Each $V_j$ is finite-dimensional and restriction maps it onto $V_{Mj}$ for every actual stabilizer $M$. With $\ker V_j=\bigcap_{v\in V_j}\ker v$, the subgroup $$N=\bigcap_j\bigl(S_{\ell j}\cap\ker V_j\bigr) \tag{K2}\label{kernel:N}$$ is normal in $D$, has finite index in $S$, and satisfies $$M\cap N =\bigcap_j\left(M_{\ell j}\cap \bigcap_{v\in V_{Mj}}\ker v\right). \tag{K3}\label{kernel:local-N}$$ The equality uses no simultaneous surjectivity across different $j$.
  - Explanation: Individual restriction surjections identify global and local annihilator kernels exactly.
- **claim-outgoing-graph-covers** (construction, [source](#stmt-kernel-graph-cover)): Let $M$ be an incidence group embedded in a free actual row and represented by its finite Stallings core. A component $L_H$ of the cover determined by $M^0$ may be required to have arbitrarily large prescribed girth. It has a nonempty finite family of connected cyclic $\ell$-covers $L_{\ell j}$, corresponding to $M_{\ell j}$. The component $L_N$ determined by $M\cap N$ is exactly the cover whose fundamental group is the intersection of the covering kernels and the kernels of every additive first-cohomology class in the nontrivial deck part of each $L_{\ell j}$, over the finite field $\mathbb k$ with $\operatorname{char}\mathbb k\ne\ell$.* *In particular, if $e_1,e_2$ are two lifts to $L_{\ell j}$ of the same oriented edge of $L_H$, the pullback to $L_N$ of $e_1^*-e_2^*$ has zero period on every closed path. All these statements are invariant under the required coset and conjugation changes.
  - Explanation: The exact kernel realizes the full cyclic-cover and nontrivial-mode annihilator intersection.
- **claim-exact-cyclic-orders** (theorem, [source](#stmt-kernel-orders)): For every specified generator $a\in S$, let $m_a$ be its order in $D/H$. Its order in $S/N$ is exactly $m_a\ell$. For every specified pair of actual noncommensurate cyclics, their images in $S/N$ have trivial intersection. Thus the prescribed evenness, largeness, and divisibility of cyclic orders survive the construction.
  - Explanation: Deck evaluations determine exact orders and exclude intersections of specified noncommensurate cyclic images.
- **claim-simultaneous-compatible-kernels** (construction, [source](#stmt-kernel-construction)): For the finite orbit list of periodic peripherals and any added maximal cyclic peripherals, all the preceding choices can be made simultaneously and equivariantly. The resulting $N_D\unlhd D$ have finite index in $S_D$, satisfy every prescribed finite membership, product, avoidance, girth and cyclic-order requirement, and give the exact local graph covers of Corollary <a href="#kernel:graph-cover" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="kernel:graph-cover">110</a>. Specified noncommensurate cyclic intersections remain exact; commensurate cyclic intersections satisfy the usual intersection identity in a finite cyclic quotient.
  - Explanation: One simultaneous equivariant choice meets all finite requests and preserves exact local covers.
- **claim-central-component-presentation** (construction, [source](#stmt-fan-components)): The developed presentation of $J$ can be arranged as a tree of central components with the following properties.* 1. *A central component has a bipartite tree of groups, with finite-rank free groups $F$ at one class of nodes and internal peripheral groups $P_d$ at the other. Each incidence group is a nontrivial finitely generated subgroup $M\le P_d$ embedded in its neighboring $F$.* 2. *Each edge between central components has infinite cyclic group $\langle c\rangle$. At one end it attaches to an internal node $d$; at the other it attaches in a different central component. Distinct outgoing incidences at the same $d$ have distinct target components.* 3. *The unused relative occurrences are cyclic. We call them outer occurrences. Internal and outer nodes together label the actual peripheral cosets, without duplication. The developed data have finite quotient by $J$.* *Every included $S_d$ has a central incidence. The added cyclic root nodes have their root incidences. Elementary filled rows may be omitted from the wall construction.
  - Explanation: Free-node incidences and cyclic component edges organize all actual peripheral occurrences without duplication.
- **claim-filled-fan-model** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fan-filled-model)): For sufficiently deep choices, $\overline{\mathcal X}$ is simply connected and $\mathcal A$ is uniformly hyperbolic. The action of $\bar J=J/K_J$ is cocompact, has free regular vertices and oriented edges, and has exact finite apex stabilizers $\bar P=P/N_P$. For each fixed filling, $\mathcal A$ is locally finite and proper, and $\bar J$ is hyperbolic.* *The central link $L_N(d)$ at an internal apex is the disjoint union of its incidence subtrees modulo $N_P$. Its components are exactly the Stallings covers determined by $M\cap N_P$. Satellite arms become indexed path cycles of period $n=\|\bar c\|$; an outer apex has its one indexed boundary cycle. Period is measured in generator steps, with bounded fractional offsets within the chosen word path.
  - Explanation: Apex-generated kernels preserve simple connectivity and give a proper cocompact hyperbolic fan model.
- **claim-finite-angle-dictionary** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fan-angle-dictionary)): All of the following conditions can be imposed for any finite list of bounds before choosing the filling.* 1. *There are no self-spokes. Two distinct central spokes from a fixed apex do not end at the same physical horizontal midpoint, and likewise do not end at the same ordinary site.* 2. *For each $R$, after the first germ is normalized to a fixed representative, every second germ at angle at most $R$ is obtained by a translator from a fixed finite list in the original peripheral group. The list includes the two germ types and does not depend on the filling. Consequently angular balls have uniformly bounded cardinality.* 3. *On one indexed arm, source germs at bounded angle have sites whose cyclic period coordinates differ by a uniformly bounded amount.* 4. *Every bounded closed walk in which each apex is visited at most once cyclically has a closed labeled lift to the original fan graph, with its given edge types and projected incidences.* 5. *All arm orders used here can be chosen even and arbitrarily large.
  - Explanation: Original finite avoidance tests control tagged germs, angular balls, cycle coordinates, and bounded lifts.
- **claim-exact-link-cover-data** (construction, [source](#stmt-fan-cover-data)): Let $H_P$ be the intersection of a periodic peripheral’s normal base choice $H$ with $P_d$, and let $L_H(d)$ be its central link modulo $H_P$. Its finitely many components can be required to have arbitrarily large girth. Over each connected component $B$ there is a nonempty finite collection of connected cyclic $\ell$-covers $B_j\to B$, where $\ell>1$, and a finite field $\mathbb k$ with $\operatorname{char}\mathbb k\nmid\ell$. The corresponding component of $L_N(d)$ is exactly the cover associated to the intersection of* 1. *the kernels of all these cyclic covering maps; and* 2. *inside each covering kernel, the kernels of all additive first cohomology classes in the nontrivial deck part of $H^1(B_j;\mathbb k)$.* *The assertion holds also for the cyclic root incidences, whose nontrivial deck cohomology part is zero.
  - Explanation: Central links inherit exact cyclic-cover and nontrivial-cohomology kernel data, including cyclic roots.
- **claim-marker-forced-passage** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-fan-marker-comparison)): In a uniformly hyperbolic graph the following hold.* 1. *Geodesic legs from $s$ with sufficiently large angle concatenate to a geodesic, and every geodesic between their other endpoints passes through $s$.* 2. *Two uniform quasigeodesics from $s$ to the same finite or ideal endpoint, neither revisiting $s$, have departure germs at bounded angle. If a geodesic has a sufficiently large interior angle at $s$, a uniform comparison quasigeodesic cannot avoid $s$. Nor can all its germs at $s$ have a previously prescribed bounded angular diameter.* 3. *Suppose uniform quasi-isometrically embedded tree pieces are joined by switches whose spokes have uniformly bounded lengths. A switch maps to a marker in the graph. For every reduced incidence path, assume each connector through a piece has distinct endpoint markers and avoids them except at its endpoints. Impose the same conditions on partial connectors at marked-node endpoints. Assume also that each piece attaches at most once at a given marker, and that all distinct spoke germs at each switch have pairwise angle larger than a sufficiently large fixed threshold. Then the joined components are uniformly quasi-isometrically embedded trees. Their node projections are injective provided the piece node projections are injective and the stated endpoint conditions hold. Every interior switch on a reduced path is a large-angle turn on a geodesic between its projected endpoints. The same conclusion holds towards an ideal endpoint of a ray when the ambient graph is proper.* *The quasi-isometry constants in the third assertion can be fixed after one minimum angle threshold is met. Increasing the angle threshold later increases the forced comparison angle without changing those constants.
  - Explanation: Large-angle switches force geodesic passage and preserve embedded tree structure.
- **claim-sparse-central-panels** (construction, [source](#stmt-fan-sparse-panels)): Fix $K$, a bound $q$ on the number of target link vertices, and a bound $r$ on the number of prescribed directions at an internal apex. There is a bound $B$, depending only on these bounds and the fixed original data, with the following property after suitable kernel choices. For every such target list and direction list there is a partition of the targets into classes, each in one component of $L_N$ and of intrinsic diameter at most $B$, such that every binary assignment to these classes extends to a central panel. Its cut germs are pairwise at angle greater than $K$, and all are at angle greater than $K$ from the prescribed directions.
