The same partition works for all binary assignments.* *There are also fillers: for every occurrence of a link edge there is a panel cutting that occurrence whose cuts all lie over its one base edge in $L_H$. Its cut germs can be required pairwise farther than $K$.
  - Explanation: Exact cover potentials separate bounded target classes with sparse angularly avoiding cuts.
- **claim-central-panel-slot-trees** (construction, [source](#stmt-fan-central-trees)): Every component $W_0$ of the panel–slot graph is a uniformly quasi-isometrically embedded tree in $\mathcal A$, injective on node projections. Its constants require only a minimum cut-angle threshold and remain valid when subsequent panel systems use larger thresholds. There are finitely many decorated node and edge orbits. Distinct systems may be retained separately as a finite labeled pool.
  - Explanation: Matched panels and midpoint slots form uniformly embedded trees with injective node projections.
- **claim-central-cocycles** (construction, [source](#stmt-fan-central-cochain)): Each $W_0$ carries an equivariant mod-two cochain $\tau_0^{W_0}$ on the central complex, closed on every central face. It has value one on the positive initial half of each marked horizontal edge, zero on all other horizontal halves, and value $\zeta_b(t)$ on an ordinary radial edge $d\!-\!t$ when its panel $b$ belongs to $W_0$, or zero when there is no such panel. Every edge with nonzero value has a panel or slot anchor of $W_0$ at one of its endpoints.
  - Explanation: Panel labels and marked horizontal halves satisfy every central triangle equation.
- **claim-satellite-arm-exclusivity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-fan-arm-exclusivity)): If $W_0$ has a node anchored on a satellite arm of $d$, then it has no node over $d$ and no anchor on a different satellite arm of the same $d$. All its anchor occurrences on that arm, and all nonzero occurrences of $\tau_0^{W_0}$ on its boundary cycle, lie in a period interval of uniformly bounded diameter. These bounds are independent of the arm order and of later increases in cut separation.* *If $\tau_0^{W_0}$ has odd total on the arm cycle, its stabilizer inside $\bar P_d$ is trivial.
  - Explanation: A central tree encounters only one arm at a source, with bounded support and trivial odd-side stabilizer.
- **claim-odd-satellite-seeds** (construction, [source](#stmt-fan-odd-seeds)): A finite pool of central panel systems, chosen at successive fixed angle scales, can be required to contain, on every satellite arm, a central tree $W_0$ for which $\tau_0^{W_0}$ has odd total on the arm’s boundary cycle. The choices and all support bounds are independent of the sufficiently large individual cycle orders.
  - Explanation: Successive fixed-scale tests produce odd arm evaluations through preserved winding parity.
- **claim-satellite-label-profiles** (construction, [source](#stmt-boundary-satellite-profiles)): Fix bounds on the number of target ordinary satellite sites and forbidden germ directions at $d$, and fix an angular avoidance threshold. A finite pool containing the odd seeds of Proposition <a href="#fan:odd-seeds" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fan:odd-seeds">123</a> supplies satellite-only panels whose labels realize every binary assignment to a partition of the target list into classes. Each class lies on one arm and has bounded cyclic period-coordinate diameter. Their spoke germs avoid the forbidden directions and one another by the prescribed threshold. The class-diameter bound and the required filling tests depend only on these fixed requests and the original finite data.
  - Explanation: Separated odd-seed placements realize arbitrary binary assignments on bounded cyclic target classes.
- **claim-equivariant-odd-side-consumption** (construction, [source](#stmt-boundary-consumption)): After taking finitely many labeled copies of a finite pool of central systems, every odd side can be consumed exactly once. This can be done equivariantly, with finitely many decorated panel and edge orbits, while including all the tests of Lemma <a href="#boundary:satellite-profiles" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="boundary:satellite-profiles">125</a> and any fixed lower bound on switch angles.
  - Explanation: Labeled multiplicities and antipodal pair panels consume each odd incidence exactly once equivariantly.
- **claim-internal-trees-cocycles** (construction, [source](#stmt-boundary-internal-trees)): The $W_1$ are uniformly quasi-isometrically embedded trees, injective on projected nodes. Each contains at most one total panel over a given internal apex. They carry equivariant cocycles $\tau_1$ on the internal graph, closed on all central and satellite fan triangles. A nonzero value on a satellite radial edge $s\to t$ has one of the following explanations:* 1. *$W_1$ contains its total panel at $s$;* 2. *a constituent $W_0$ has an anchor on that arm within a uniformly bounded period-coordinate distance from $t$, accessible from $t$ by a short internal boundary arc.* *The bounds, and the quasi-isometry constants, depend only on minimum bend requirements and the basic central support bounds. Increasing subsequent angular separations does not increase these constants.
  - Explanation: Satellite switches extend central trees and cocycles while keeping all defaults locally anchored.
- **claim-outer-support-clusters** (theorem, [source](#stmt-boundary-outer-clusters)): For a fixed $W_1$, the nonzero positions of $\tau_1$ on the boundary cycle of an outer apex $p$ lie in a bounded cyclic period interval. An odd encounter has trivial stabilizer in the arm rotation group. The interval bound is independent of later increases in switch angles.
  - Explanation: Internal embedding and period dictionaries bound outer support and eliminate odd rotation stabilizers.
- **claim-completed-wall-trees** (construction, [source](#stmt-boundary-completed-trees)): The resulting components $W=W_2$ are uniformly quasi-isometrically embedded trees. Their $W_1$-nodes and switch nodes have distinct projections within a component. They carry cocycles $\tau_W$ on the full simply connected fan complex, supported in a uniform neighborhood of $W$. Under group transport the only ambiguity in these cocycles is a sum of vertex coboundaries at outer switches. There are finitely many decorated node and edge orbits.
  - Explanation: Outer pair switches complete embedded trees with cocycles ambiguous only by outer vertex coboundaries.
- **claim-cocycle-boundary-sides** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-boundary-sides)): For each $W$, its stabilizer is quasiconvex in $\bar J$ and acts cocompactly on $W$. The cocycle defines a locally constant binary coloring on $\partial\bar J\setminus\Lambda W$. Its stabilizer preserves the two colors up to a global flip. If two points outside $\Lambda W$ have different colors, a quasiconvex codimension-one subgroup separates them in the sense of the Bergeron–Wise criterion.
  - Explanation: Compact tree stabilizers and binary cocycle colors give quasiconvex codimension-one separators.
- **claim-bounded-outer-normalization** (construction, [source](#stmt-boundary-normalization)): Fix a bound $A_p$ on cyclic period gaps at outer turns of a bi-infinite geodesic $\gamma$. Replacing these turns by boundary arcs and making the elementary fan detours produces a pure internal uniform quasigeodesic $\alpha$. Its constants depend only on $A_p$ and the fixed data.* 1. *Each physical vertex occurs a bounded number of times on $\alpha$, and all its occurrences lie in a bounded parameter interval.* 2. *If an internal apex $d$ lies on $\gamma$, all new germs at $d$ lie within bounded angular distance of one of its two original germs $\nu_-,\nu_+$. When these are sufficiently far apart, each neighborhood contains an odd number of the new radial half-incidences.* 3. *If all original internal turns have bounded angle, then the angular diameter of all germs at all visits to any one internal apex on $\alpha$ is bounded.
  - Explanation: Bounded outer replacements preserve quasigeodesicity and control repeated visits and germ parity.
- **claim-uncontaminated-satellite-tests** (theorem, [source](#stmt-boundary-satellite-test)): At an internal apex $d$ visited by $\alpha$, apply Lemma <a href="#boundary:satellite-profiles" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="boundary:satellite-profiles">125</a> to its satellite radial site list, with spoke germs far from every $d$-direction of $\alpha$. The resulting tree through $T$ evaluates on $\alpha$ exactly as the prescribed satellite labels on that list. In the line setting its limit set avoids both ideal endpoints. If all such evaluations are even, the satellite radial half-incidences can be paired within their classes and replaced by bounded purely central boundary arcs avoiding $d$.
  - Explanation: Avoiding first directions isolates satellite labels and permits bounded replacements when every test is even.
- **claim-large-internal-turn-separation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-boundary-large-internal)): In the line setting, a sufficiently large original internal turn of $\gamma$ is separated by one of the constructed trees. The required turn threshold $A_d$ is chosen after the satellite replacement bound $B_s$ and before the regular-case tests below.
  - Explanation: Nonmixed central tests separate a large original internal turn without satellite contamination.
- **claim-regular-comparison-connectors** (theorem, [source](#stmt-boundary-regular-comparisons)): Sites participating in $\alpha^1$ have bounded connectors to true ordinary sites of $\alpha$. Comparisons between them have uniformly bounded cumulative germ diameter at every internal apex. In the line setting, they avoid outer apices, are uniform quasigeodesics, and extend to either ideal endpoint. The lists needed at any tested internal apex have bounded size. These assertions persist after adding any fixed bounded horizontal tails to the connectors.
  - Explanation: Bounded replacement tails preserve comparison geometry and finite tested site lists.
- **claim-regular-central-parity-tests** (theorem, [source](#stmt-boundary-central-test)): At an internal apex $s$ with radial halves in $\alpha^1$, central panel tests evaluate exactly the class parities of their ordinary target sites. An odd test separates the ideal endpoints in the line setting and gives an odd $W_1$-total on the outer cycle in the circle setting. Otherwise all remaining radial halves can be paired and replaced by bounded horizontal link paths, giving a purely horizontal chain $\alpha^2$.
  - Explanation: Isolated central labels either separate directly or permit bounded horizontal replacements.
- **claim-surviving-horizontal-parity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-boundary-horizontal-parity)): The chain $\alpha^2$ contains a physical horizontal edge with odd multiplicity. A final central system whose cut and switch thresholds exceed the new regular comparison bounds has a slot tree with odd total on this chain. In the line setting its limit set avoids both ideal endpoints.
  - Explanation: Winding or end-crossing parity leaves an odd physical edge detected by a final slot tree.
- **claim-odd-outer-encounters** (construction, [source](#stmt-boundary-outer-odd-seeds)): A finite pool of $W_1$-systems contains, on the cycle of every outer apex, at least one $W_1$ with odd total. The pool and all its required bounds can be fixed before the final filling depth choices.
  - Explanation: Circle tests supply odd internal-tree encounters independently of outer boundary separation.
- **claim-large-outer-gap-separation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-boundary-large-outer)): A sufficiently large cyclic period gap at an outer turn of a geodesic $\gamma$ is separated by one of the completed trees. The gap threshold $A_p$ depends only on the basic quasi-isometry and support-cluster bounds, not on later increased switch bends.
  - Explanation: Rotated antipodal odd clusters separate a large outer gap with controlled first directions.
- **claim-full-boundary-separation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-boundary-separation)): There are finitely many systems of completed trees such that every pair of distinct points of $\partial\bar J$ lies outside the limit set of one of the trees and has different cocycle colors there.
  - Explanation: Large outer, large internal, and regular configurations together separate all distinct boundary pairs.
- **claim-noncircular-scale-order** (construction, [source](#stmt-boundary-scale-order)): All systems used above can be chosen from a finite pool by finitely many original depth, angle, girth, period-order, and avoidance tests. These tests can be imposed simultaneously with any initial filling-depth request and the finite-path tests of Section <a href="#sec:transfer-relative" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:transfer-relative">14</a>.
  - Explanation: A finite ordered sequence fixes geometric thresholds before the final kernel choices.
- **claim-special-filled-vertices** (theorem, [source](#stmt-boundary-filled-vertices)): For the terminal row and peripheral data constructed in Sections <a href="#sec:07-transfer" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:07-transfer">13</a>–<a href="#sec:09-fans" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:09-fans">16</a>, one can choose the height-fiber kernels arbitrarily deep, simultaneously satisfying the finite-path tests, so that every filled vertex group $\bar J$ is hyperbolic and virtually compact special.
  - Explanation: Boundary separators cubulate the filled rows and yield compact special finite covers.
- **claim-arbitrarily-deep-good-quotients** (construction, [source](#stmt-boundary-good-fillings)): Let $G$ be the hyperbolic torsion-free primitive extension group under consideration, with the terminal finite malnormal quasiconvex virtually compact special peripheral family constructed in the preceding sections. For every prescribed sufficiently deep filling-avoidance request, there is a filling of this family to a hyperbolic virtually compact special quotient. Its peripheral images are finite-by-cyclic or finite, are hyperbolic virtually compact special, and have the inherited relative peripheral structure and filling conclusions.
  - Explanation: Transferred quasiconvex splittings assemble the compact-special filled vertices into good ambient quotients.
- **claim-primitive-extension-specialness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-boundary-primitive-vcs)): Every hyperbolic torsion-free primitive extension group of either of Linton’s two forms specified in the introduction is virtually compact special.
  - Explanation: The primitive field setup and good quotients satisfy the recovery criterion.
- **claim-virtual-free-by-cyclic-embedding** (theorem, [source](#stmt-cor-free-by-cyclic)): Let $G$ be one of the following groups.* 1. *A one-relator group $$G=F(X)/\langle\!\langle r\rangle\!\rangle,$$ where $X$ is finite and $r\in F(X)$ is arbitrary, such that either $G$ is word-hyperbolic or $G$ contains no subgroup isomorphic to $\mathrm{BS}(m,n)$ for any nonzero integers $m,n$.* 2. *A word-hyperbolic ascending mapping torus $$G=\langle F,t\mid t^{-1}ft=\phi(f)\ (f\in F)\rangle,$$ where $F$ is a free group of finite rank and $\phi:F\to F$ is injective.* *There are a finite-index subgroup $H\leq G$, an integer $d\geq0$, an automorphism $\alpha$ of the rank-$d$ free group $F_d$, and an embedding $$H\hookrightarrow F_d\rtimes_\alpha\mathbb Z.$$ In particular, $G$ is virtually free-by-cyclic: the same $H$ fits into an exact sequence $$1\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow H\longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow1, \qquad K\text{ free},\quad Q\leq\mathbb Z.$$ The rank of $K$ may be infinite, and $Q$ may be trivial.
  - Explanation: The stated group classes virtually embed in finite-rank free-by-cyclic groups; their own free kernels may have infinite rank.

        "anchor": "stmt-row-path-inertia",
        "exact_quote": "In $T$ and $T_0$, every path with noncyclic pointwise stabilizer is monotone.         "anchor": "stmt-row-boundary-gates",
        "exact_quote": "Let a torsion-free hyperbolic group $J$ act cocompactly on a tree of hyperbolic Cayley spaces with uniformly quasi-isometrically embedded edge maps and hyperbolic total space. We use the standard Cayley realization with uniformly proper vertex inclusions and isometric product strips over open edges. For the finite splittings here, properness is uniform: normalize a vertex to the identity and take the maximum intrinsic length of the finitely many elements in each ambient word ball, over the finitely many vertex types. Let $A\\leq J$ preserve a connected subtree $Y$, with $A\\backslash Y$ finite. Suppose its vertex and edge stabilizers are finitely generated and quasiconvex in the respective rows. Either of the following suffices for $A$ to be quasiconvex in $J$:*\n\n1.  *ambient vertex rows are quasiconvex in $J$;*\n\n2.  *every edge leaving $Y$ intersects $A$ trivially or cyclically.*\n\n*This applies in particular to $G$ acting on $T$ or $T_0$.",

        "anchor": "stmt-row-period-rule",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose $A\\leq G$, $h(A)\\neq0$, and $$S=A\\cap L,\\qquad 0<\\beta(S)<\\infty.$$ At every actual level $\\mathscr L$, inclusion induces an isomorphism $$\\bigoplus_{\\xi\\in S\\backslash\\mathscr L}\n H_1(S\\cap X_\\xi;D_S)\\ \\longrightarrow\\ H_1(S;D_S).$$ Both incident edge-level maps to a vertex level are isomorphisms. Every level sum therefore has dimension $q_X=\\beta(S)$. The convex hull $Y$ of the rows with noncyclic $S\\cap X_\\xi$ contains no edge with trivial $S$-stabilizer.         "anchor": "stmt-coeff-extraction",
        "exact_quote": "Let finitely many normalized rational expressions have hereditary offsets in a finitely generated subgroup $H$, and let $\\chi\\colon H\\twoheadrightarrow\\mathbb Z$ be a character with kernel $K$. Expand in the positive skew Laurent field in <a href=\"#coeff:cyclic-field\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"coeff:cyclic-field\">[coeff:cyclic-field]</a>, writing powers of $t$ on the right. Every coefficient has a finite normalized rational expression in $D_K$, with the following properties.*\n\n1.  *If a summand is permitted on $S$, the expression for its coefficient of degree $n$ has term patterns contained in $$(S\\cap\\chi^{-1}(n))t^{-n}.$$ Here $S$ can be replaced by its intersection with $H$.*\n\n2.  *Coefficient extraction does not increase the complexity of an arbitrary top expression. If an inverse occurrence is nonhomogeneous, the decrease is strict. In particular, for a normalized operand $P$ whose hereditary offsets are not all killed by $\\chi$, every coefficient expression has complexity strictly less than $c(P)$.*\n\n3.  *For a collection of top expressions, assume at least one represented top offset equals $1$ and that $\\chi$ is nonzero on the subgroup generated by all their hereditary offsets. The joint complexity of the coefficient expressions at each degree is strictly smaller than the original joint complexity.*\n\n4.  *If the input is represented in one field coset $D_Aa$, with all inverse operands internal to $A$, a nonzero coefficient of degree $n$ is represented in one coset of $D_{A\\cap K}$. Its permitted group coset is $(Aa\\cap\\chi^{-1}(n))t^{-n}$, and its inverse operands remain internal to $A\\cap K$.",

        "anchor": "stmt-coeff-analytic-calculus",
        "exact_quote": "The affiliated algebra of a finite von Neumann algebra is complete for convergence in measure. Products of tight families are tight. If $a_j\\to0$ in measure and $b_j,c_j$ range over tight families, then $b_ja_jc_j\\to0$ in measure. These assertions also hold uniformly over an additional index.*\n\n*Positive square roots are continuous in measure on positive affiliated operators, and inversion is continuous in measure on positive affiliated units.         "anchor": "stmt-gate-capture",
        "exact_quote": "Unless $G$ is already virtually compact special by the acylindrical case, there is an invariant system of actual objects, finite modulo $G$, with full stabilizers $A$ and kernels $S=A\\cap L$, having these properties:*\n\n1.  *$h(A)\\ne0$; each $A$ is quasiconvex, virtually compact special, and field-acyclic.*\n\n2.  *Each $S$ is a nested union of finite-rank free approximants of one constant rank at least two. Distinct actual object stabilizers intersect in at most cyclic groups.*\n\n4.  *There is a uniform length such that the pointwise stabilizer of every longer noncyclically stabilized actual path, in $T_0$ or in the refined tree $T$, is wholly contained in one of these kernels $S$.",

Its field first-homology dimension is positive and finite, and its ambient homology detects every noncyclic subgroup.*\n\n3.  *For representatives of the actual object orbits under $L$, the maps $$\\bigoplus H_1(S;D_L)\\longrightarrow H_1(L;D_L)$$ are jointly injective. Distinct actual object stabilizers intersect in at most cyclic groups.*\n\n4.  *There is a uniform length such that the pointwise stabilizer of every longer noncyclically stabilized actual path, in $T_0$ or in the refined tree $T$, is wholly contained in one of these kernels $S$.",

      "exact_statement": "Unless $G$ is already virtually compact special by the acylindrical case, there is an invariant system of actual objects, finite modulo $G$, with full stabilizers $A$ and kernels $S=A\\cap L$, having these properties:*\n\n1.  *$h(A)\\ne0$; each $A$ is quasiconvex, virtually compact special, and field-acyclic.*\n\n2.  *Each $S$ is a nested union of finite-rank free approximants of one constant rank at least two.         "anchor": "stmt-transfer-finite-path-transfer",
        "exact_quote": "Fix an integer $n$. Its stabilizer is exactly the image of the actual path stabilizer.*\n\n3.  *Taking $n$ at least the terminal path bound, the resulting Bass–Serre action is acylindrical: sufficiently long segment stabilizers are finite of uniformly bounded order. Each filled row is hyperbolic and each edge map is quasi-isometric.*\n\n*Here the ambient filled group is hyperbolic by sufficiently long filling of the original relatively hyperbolic pair: the periodic peripheral reductions are finite-by-cyclic and hence hyperbolic, and the additional cyclic reductions are finite.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-transfer-coset-projection",
        "exact_quote": "Fix finitely many quasiconvex subgroup types in a hyperbolic group $J$, with its ordinary Cayley metric. There are uniform constants $R,C$ with the following property. For types $H,K$ and a coset $gK$, either the projection of $H$ to $gK$ has diameter at most $C$, or there are $h\\in H,k\\in K$ such that $$w=h^{-1}gk,\\qquad |w|\\le R.$$ After translation by $h^{-1}$, that projection lies within distance $C$ of $(H\\cap wKw^{-1})w$. Thus the unbounded alternative involves only finitely many normalized intersection types. These intersections are quasiconvex in the row and in the corresponding attaching group.",
        "source_id": "PM-258.2"

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-kernel-graph-cover",
        "exact_quote": "Let $M$ be an incidence group embedded in a free actual row and represented by its finite Stallings core. A component $L_H$ of the cover determined by $M^0$ may be required to have arbitrarily large prescribed girth. It has a nonempty finite family of connected cyclic $\\ell$-covers $L_{\\ell j}$, corresponding to $M_{\\ell j}$. The component $L_N$ determined by $M\\cap N$ is exactly the cover whose fundamental group is the intersection of the covering kernels and the kernels of every additive first-cohomology class in the nontrivial deck part of each $L_{\\ell j}$, over the finite field $\\mathbb k$ with $\\operatorname{char}\\mathbb k\\ne\\ell$.*\n\n*In particular, if $e_1,e_2$ are two lifts to $L_{\\ell j}$ of the same oriented edge of $L_H$, the pullback to $L_N$ of $e_1^*-e_2^*$ has zero period on every closed path. All these statements are invariant under the required coset and conjugation changes.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-fan-components",
        "exact_quote": "The developed presentation of $J$ can be arranged as a tree of central components with the following properties.*\n\n1.  *A central component has a bipartite tree of groups, with finite-rank free groups $F$ at one class of nodes and internal peripheral groups $P_d$ at the other. Each incidence group is a nontrivial finitely generated subgroup $M\\le P_d$ embedded in its neighboring $F$.*\n\n2.  *Each edge between central components has infinite cyclic group $\\langle c\\rangle$. At one end it attaches to an internal node $d$; at the other it attaches in a different central component. Distinct outgoing incidences at the same $d$ have distinct target components.*\n\n3.  *The unused relative occurrences are cyclic. We call them outer occurrences. Internal and outer nodes together label the actual peripheral cosets, without duplication. The developed data have finite quotient by $J$.*\n\n*Every included $S_d$ has a central incidence.         "exact_quote": "For sufficiently deep choices, $\\overline{\\mathcal X}$ is simply connected and $\\mathcal A$ is uniformly hyperbolic.         "anchor": "stmt-fan-angle-dictionary",
        "exact_quote": "All of the following conditions can be imposed for any finite list of bounds before choosing the filling.*\n\n1.  *There are no self-spokes. Two distinct central spokes from a fixed apex do not end at the same physical horizontal midpoint, and likewise do not end at the same ordinary site.*\n\n2.  *For each $R$, after the first germ is normalized to a fixed representative, every second germ at angle at most $R$ is obtained by a translator from a fixed finite list in the original peripheral group. The list includes the two germ types and does not depend on the filling. Consequently angular balls have uniformly bounded cardinality.*\n\n3.  *On one indexed arm, source germs at bounded angle have sites whose cyclic period coordinates differ by a uniformly bounded amount.*\n\n4.  *Every bounded closed walk in which each apex is visited at most once cyclically has a closed labeled lift to the original fan graph, with its given edge types and projected incidences.*\n\n5.  *All arm orders used here can be chosen even and arbitrarily large.",

          "exact_quote": "All of the following conditions can be imposed for any finite list of bounds before choosing the filling.*\n\n1.  *There are no self-spokes. Two distinct central spokes from a fixed apex do not end at the same physical horizontal midpoint, and likewise do not end at the same ordinary site.*\n\n2.  *For each $R$, after the first germ is normalized to a fixed representative, every second germ at angle at most $R$ is obtained by a translator from a fixed finite list in the original peripheral group. The list includes the two germ types and does not depend on the filling. Consequently angular balls have uniformly bounded cardinality.*\n\n3.  *On one indexed arm, source germs at bounded angle have sites whose cyclic period coordinates differ by a uniformly bounded amount.*\n\n4.  *Every bounded closed walk in which each apex is visited at most once cyclically has a closed labeled lift to the original fan graph, with its given edge types and projected incidences.*\n\n5.  *All arm orders used here can be chosen even and arbitrarily large.",
          "source_id": "PM-258.2"
        }

        "exact_quote": "Let $H_P$ be the intersection of a periodic peripheral’s normal base choice $H$ with $P_d$, and let $L_H(d)$ be its central link modulo $H_P$.         "anchor": "stmt-fan-marker-comparison",
        "exact_quote": "<span id=\"fan:marker\" label=\"fan:marker\"></span>In a uniformly hyperbolic graph the following hold.*\n\n1.  *Geodesic legs from $s$ with sufficiently large angle concatenate to a geodesic, and every geodesic between their other endpoints passes through $s$.*\n\n2.  *Two uniform quasigeodesics from $s$ to the same finite or ideal endpoint, neither revisiting $s$, have departure germs at bounded angle. If a geodesic has a sufficiently large interior angle at $s$, a uniform comparison quasigeodesic cannot avoid $s$. Nor can all its germs at $s$ have a previously prescribed bounded angular diameter.*\n\n3.  *Suppose uniform quasi-isometrically embedded tree pieces are joined by switches whose spokes have uniformly bounded lengths. A switch maps to a marker in the graph. For every reduced incidence path, assume each connector through a piece has distinct endpoint markers and avoids them except at its endpoints. Impose the same conditions on partial connectors at marked-node endpoints. Assume also that each piece attaches at most once at a given marker, and that all distinct spoke germs at each switch have pairwise angle larger than a sufficiently large fixed threshold. Then the joined components are uniformly quasi-isometrically embedded trees. Their node projections are injective provided the piece node projections are injective and the stated endpoint conditions hold. Every interior switch on a reduced path is a large-angle turn on a geodesic between its projected endpoints. The same conclusion holds towards an ideal endpoint of a ray when the ambient graph is proper.*\n\n*The quasi-isometry constants in the third assertion can be fixed after one minimum angle threshold is met. Increasing the angle threshold later increases the forced comparison angle without changing those constants.",

        "anchor": "stmt-fan-sparse-panels",
        "exact_quote": "<span id=\"fan:central-panels\" label=\"fan:central-panels\"></span>Fix $K$, a bound $q$ on the number of target link vertices, and a bound $r$ on the number of prescribed directions at an internal apex. There is a bound $B$, depending only on these bounds and the fixed original data, with the following property after suitable kernel choices. For every such target list and direction list there is a partition of the targets into classes, each in one component of $L_N$ and of intrinsic diameter at most $B$, such that every binary assignment to these classes extends to a central panel. Its cut germs are pairwise at angle greater than $K$, and all are at angle greater than $K$ from the prescribed directions. The same partition works for all binary assignments.*\n\n*There are also fillers: for every occurrence of a link edge there is a panel cutting that occurrence whose cuts all lie over its one base edge in $L_H$. <a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Compact-special abbreviations** ([source](#sec:background)): We write VCS for *virtually compact special*, QC for quasiconvex, and fg for finitely generated.
- **Subgroup-field hypotheses** ([source](#fill:field)): We specify the division-ring hypotheses, rather than assume that local indicability alone supplies them. For a group $J$, write $D(J)$ for a division ring containing $\mathbb QJ$. Throughout this section the rings for subgroups are compatible division closures inside the ambient ring; distinct subgroup cosets are linearly independent over the corresponding subgroup division ring; and finite-index coset representatives span the ambient division ring over the subgroup division ring. We also use the following character consequence of Hughes-freeness. If $N=\ker\chi$, where $\chi$ is a real character of a finitely generated subgroup $J$, then $$D(J)=\operatorname{Ore}\bigl(D(N)*(J/N)\bigr). \label{fill:field}$$ Here the crossed product is embedded using coset representatives. Its quotient $J/N$ is finitely generated free abelian, so the crossed product is a Noetherian skew Laurent domain. These are the subgroup-field properties of the Hughes-free Linnell fields used in our applications; see [[Hughes1970](#ref-Hughes1970), [Linnell1993](#ref-Linnell1993)] for their origins and [[JaikinLopezAlvarez2020](#ref-JaikinLopezAlvarez2020), Corollaries 6.2–6.3] and [[JaikinUniversality2021](#ref-JaikinUniversality2021), Section 2.3 and Proposition 2.2] for the locally indicable affiliated realization and the normal-subgroup crossed-product assertions. Arbitrary subgroup coset independence is justified separately at the start of Section <a href="#sec:04-coefficients" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:04-coefficients">6</a>. We refer to this collection of properties as the *subgroup-field hypotheses*.
- **Ordinary positive Novikov completion** ([source](#fill:novikov-ring)): $$\widehat{\mathbb QJ}^{\,\chi} =\left\{\sum_{g\in J}a_g g: \#\{g:a_g\ne0,\ \chi(g)<c\}<\infty \text{ for every }c\in\mathbb R\right\}. \label{fill:novikov-ring}$$ Our completion convention is towards positive height. The subgroup-field hypotheses embed $D(J)$ and this ring in the same skew series division ring over $D(\ker\chi)$. Indeed, <a href="#fill:field" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="fill:field">[fill:field]</a> embeds the rational field there; a nonzero series has a leading term, and its positive remainder has a positive minimum valuation, so geometric inversion is defined. This remains valid when $\chi(J)$ is dense in $\mathbb R$, because the support condition is finite below each threshold.
- **Selective realization property** ([source](#stmt-fill-selective-input)): Let $K\lhd J$, with $J/K$ virtually RFRS. We say that $(J,K)$ has the *selective realization property* if, for every finite-index preimage $J'\le J$ and every finite set $T\subset K$, there are a finite-index preimage $H\le J'$, normal in $J'$, a subgroup $U\le K$ containing $T$, and a homomorphism from $H$ to a virtually RFRS group that is injective on $U$.
- **Ascending mapping torus and height** ([source](#sec:02-ascending)): For an injective endomorphism $\phi:F\to F$, write $$J_\phi=\langle F,t\mid t^{-1}gt=\phi(g)\ (g\in F)\rangle.$$
- **Primitive extension data** ([source](#stmt-row-primitive-data)): Fix $k\geq1$, set $a_i=t^{-i}at^i$, and put $$B_0=\{a_1,\ldots,a_{k-1}\},\qquad P_-=F(a_0,\ldots,a_{k-1}),\qquad P_+=F(a_1,\ldots,a_k).$$ An empty $B_0$ is allowed. For relatively prime positive integers $p,q$, write $\operatorname{pr}_{p/q}(v,w)$ for the positive primitive word of slope $p/q$ in two slots. The two presentations are $$\label{row:primitive-presentations} G=\langle a,t\mid R\rangle,\qquad R=\operatorname{pr}_{p/q}(x,y) \quad\hbox{or}\quad R=\operatorname{pr}_{p/q}(xy,z),$$ where $$x\in P_-\setminus F(B_0),\qquad y\in P_+\setminus F(B_0),\qquad 1\neq z\in F(B_0)$$ (the last choice is needed only in the second form). We assume that $G$ is torsion-free and hyperbolic and that the word has Linton’s primitive exceptional property [[LintonHyperbolic2026](#ref-LintonHyperbolic2026), Sections 3.1 and 5]. Explicitly, for the first form the family $\{\langle x\rangle,\langle y\rangle\}$ is malnormal in the free group on $a_0,\ldots,a_k$; if $p=q=1$, the same word must not admit a factorization $x'y'$, with $x',y'$ on the respective sides outside $F(B_0)$, whose cyclic family is nonmalnormal. In the second form $\langle z\rangle$ is malnormal; if $p/q$ is an integer, the displayed word must not admit such a factorization $x'y'$. Inversions can be absorbed into the slots.
- **Linnell fields and field homology** ([source](#stmt-row-coefficients)): For $U\leq G$, let $D_U$ be the rational Linnell division field inside the affiliated-operator algebra $\mathcal U(U)$. Local indicability and the strong Atiyah theorem give these compatible Hughes-free fields [[Brodskii1984](#ref-Brodskii1984), [Howie1982](#ref-Howie1982), [JaikinLopezAlvarez2020](#ref-JaikinLopezAlvarez2020)]. We use natural subgroup embeddings, independence of distinct cosets over subgroup fields, and rational skew-Laurent extension over the kernel of a cyclic quotient [[JaikinUniversality2021](#ref-JaikinUniversality2021), Section 2.3 and Proposition 2.2]. Coset independence also holds for affiliated coefficients: clear finitely many coefficients to bounded subgroup operators and use their disjoint Fourier supports. For $V\leq U$, $H_*(V;D_U)$ uses right group multiplication on coefficients and left vector spaces; equivalently compute over $D_V$ and extend scalars. Put $$\beta(V)=\dim_{D_V}H_1(V;D_V).$$ This dimension is unchanged by overfield extension. For a nontrivial free group of finite rank $r$, it is $r-1$; for an infinitely generated free group it is infinite; for the trivial group it is zero. Coefficients precede chain vectors and boundary matrices act on the right. Write $d(v)$ for the Fox one-chain of a word $v$, so that $$d(vw)=d(v)+v\,d(w),\qquad \partial d(v)=v-1,\qquad \Delta(v)=(v-1)^{-1}d(v)\quad(v\neq1).$$ Thus $\partial\Delta(v)=1$, and $\Delta(v)-\Delta(w)$ is a cycle. Intrinsic expressions are taken modulo two-boundaries. A subgroup *detects* a noncyclic subgroup in ambient homology if some such difference from the latter subgroup has nonzero class. Changing an orbit representative by $s$ conjugates the group symbols by $s$ and right-multiplies their coefficients by $s^{-1}$. Conjugation of symbols and coefficients acts on ambient homology by left multiplication by $s$, so this convention preserves ambient classes. Differentiating $svs^{-1}$ gives the same verification: connecting-path terms cancel for a cycle.
- **Permitted algebraic support** ([source](#pm-h-25)): A *support pattern* is a subset of $J$ of the form $$\mathcal P=A_1g_1A_2g_2\cdots A_mg_m, \qquad A_i\le J,\quad g_i\in J.$$ A product $d_1g_1\cdots d_mg_m$, where $d_i\in D_{A_i}$, is *permitted on* $\mathcal P$. For $S\subseteq J$, let $\mathcal V(S)$ be the $\mathbb Q$-span of all such products whose support pattern is contained in $S$. These are permitted algebraic supports; no choice of a scalar-function realization is involved in the definition.
- **Hereditary offsets and ordinal complexity** ([source](#coeff:complexity)): Write $\oplus$ for natural, or Hessenberg, addition of ordinals: add the coefficients of equal powers in Cantor normal form. Define the *path weight* and *complexity* recursively by $$\begin{aligned} w(qP_1^{-1}\cdots P_s^{-1}g) &=\bigoplus_{i=1}^s\omega^{c(P_i)},\label{coeff:path-weight}\\ c(E)&=\bigoplus_{T\text{ a displayed term of }E}\omega^{w(T)}. \label{coeff:complexity} \end{aligned}$$
- **Tight affiliated families** ([source](#pm-h-32)): A family $\mathcal A$ of affiliated operators is *tight* if $$\lim_{K\longrightarrow\infty} \sup_{a\in\mathcal A}\tau\bigl(1_{(K,\infty)}(\|a\|)\bigr)=0.$$
- **Positive affiliated unit and resolvent contraction** ([source](#coeff:analytic-F)): A *positive affiliated unit* in a corner is a positive affiliated operator whose support is the identity of that corner; its inverse is allowed to be unbounded. For two such units define $$\label{coeff:analytic-F} F(P,X)=P^{1/2}(P+X)^{-1}P^{1/2} =\bigl(1+P^{-1/2}XP^{-1/2}\bigr)^{-1}.$$ This is a bounded positive contraction.
- **Expansion package** ([source](#stmt-gate-package)): Consider oriented monotone paths in a tree of groups with height. Sample at successive occurrences of one edge type, and number these occurrences by integers. At position $i$ fix a short window $W_i$, of a fixed radius $s$; the window may consist of the sampled edge itself. Write $H_i=\mathop{\mathrm{Stab}}(W_i)$, with pointwise stabilizers throughout. In the relative case fix an invariant system of height-zero peripheral groups. A group is *nonparabolic* if it is nontrivial and is not contained in any one of these actual peripheral groups. The required package consists of the following properties. 1. The total tree of ordinary or relative Cayley spaces is hyperbolic, and all adjacent edge maps are uniformly quasi-isometric embeddings. 2. Nonparabolically stabilized windows of each fixed shape have finitely many orbits. The same holds for their nonparabolically stabilized extensions, including configurations with a specified common subwindow. Their stabilizers, with intrinsic relative metrics, embed quasi-isometrically in every row of the window; constants are uniform for each bounded shape. 3. A stabilizer of a window containing a short window is a free product of representatives of its nontrivial peripheral intersections and a free group, with a finite relative decomposition. The peripheral systems restrict exactly under further window restrictions. Every window group under consideration has a loxodromic element in the relevant short-window free-product trees. 4. Two distinct continuations through the same short window, with their terminal positions at the same height, have stabilizers intersecting in an at most cyclic group. For $H_i$ use the Bass tree $R_i$ of the stated free-product decomposition, with trivial edge stabilizers and finite quotient. Its elliptic subgroups are exactly the prescribed restricted peripheral subgroups. In the ordinary application $R_i$ is the horizontal free Cayley tree, and the deep-window groups under consideration are noncyclic. Relative trees may have vertices of infinite valence.
- **Admissible periodic system and budget** ([source](#stmt-close-input)): An admissible system is a $G$-invariant set of objects with finitely many $G$-orbits, whose full stabilizers $A$ satisfy the following conditions. 1. $h(A)\ne0$; $A$ is quasiconvex in $G$, virtually compact special, and acyclic over $D_A$. 2. Stabilizers of distinct objects intersect at most cyclically. 3. For $S=A\cap L$, one has $0<\beta(S)<\infty$, every noncyclic subgroup of $S$ is detected, and the natural map $$\bigoplus_{d\in L\backslash\mathcal D}H_1(S_d;D_L) \longrightarrow H_1(L;D_L)$$ is injective. Representatives and coefficient transports are taken in the convention of Section <a href="#sec:03-rows" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:03-rows">5</a>. 4. There is a fixed length such that every noncyclic stabilizer of an actual path of that length lies wholly in one of the $S_d$. The system supplied by Proposition <a href="#gate:capture" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="gate:capture">62</a> is admissible. Its *budget* is $$\mathcal B(\mathcal D)= \sum_{d\in L\backslash\mathcal D}\beta(S_d)\le k-1.$$ This is a finite sum: each $G$-orbit splits into finitely many $L$-orbits because its stabilizer has nonzero height image.
- **Exact relative embedding** ([source](#stmt-transfer-relative-embedding)): Let $J$ be hyperbolic relative to a finite list $\mathcal P$. An *exact relative embedding* of $B\le J$ means that: 1. the nontrivial groups $B\cap pPp^{-1}$, for $P\in\mathcal P$, have a finite list of representatives up to $B$-conjugacy; 2. $B$ is finitely generated relative to this list; and 3. its coned Cayley graph maps quasi-isometrically into the coned Cayley graph of $J$, with each peripheral apex sent to the corresponding actual peripheral coset. Thus the apex map is injective on actual cosets. “Exact” refers to these induced intersections; it does not require that an induced subgroup equal the ambient peripheral.
- **Peripheral compatibility tests** ([source](#stmt-transfer-finite-tests)): Fix the rows and subgroup embeddings to be tested, and a finite list of their peripheral subgroup occurrences. For each ambient peripheral $P$, a filling kernel $N_P\lhd P$ is required to satisfy the following conditions for specified finite original lists: - inside a peripheral, finite-list membership in each indicated intersection subgroup $Q$, or product $Q t R$ for a specified $t$ and indicated subgroups $Q,R$, lifts from the peripheral quotient; - $\bar Q\cap \bar s\bar R\bar s^{-1}=\overline{Q\cap sRs^{-1}}$ there for specified $s$.
- **Central panel** ([source](#pm-h-72)): A *central panel* $b$ at $d$ is a function $\zeta_b:V(L_N(d))\to\{0,1\}$, defined on all ordinary link vertices.
- **Sides and nonmixed total panels** ([source](#stmt-boundary-total-panels)): A *side* is a pair $(W_0,a)$ where the central tree $W_0$ has an anchor occurrence on the boundary of an actual satellite arm $a$ at its source $d$. The tree retains its system label and, when copies are taken, its copy index. The side is *odd* if $\tau_0^{W_0}$ has total one on the indexed boundary cycle of $a$. Consuming this side means assigning this particular incidence to one satellite panel and choosing an anchor occurrence on $a$ for its attachment. A *central-only total panel* is a central panel $b$, with no additional attachment at $d$. A *satellite-only total panel* $T$ has no central panel and consumes finitely many odd $W_0$-sides on the satellite arms at $d$, an even number on each arm. For every consumed side, attach a spoke from $T$ to its chosen anchor occurrence. The spoke projects to that tagged satellite radial edge. Its germ at $d$ is required to be far from every other spoke germ of $T$. On each satellite arm, the binary labels of $T$ are a primitive of the sum of the boundary cochains of the sides it consumes there. Such a primitive exists because the number of odd sides is even. Its additive constant is chosen independently on each arm. Central labels of $T$ are zero. Empty satellite-only panels, including their independent constant labels, are allowed.

Thus the same scalar-function map preserves the Fox boundary and divergence equations used in the closure construction. This consequence uses linearity and right equivariance; it requires no multiplicativity for division-ring coefficients.\n\nWe first make the complexity argument precise. <a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-compact-toolkit-reduction** [claim](#stmt-prop-primitive-reduction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-primitive-reduction): Separate the trivial and torsion cases, then propagate primitive terminal specialness up the truncated quasiconvex tower. -> Reduction of claim-one-relator-specialness to primitive extensions
- **step-selective-cubical-geometry** [claim](#stmt-fill-selective) / [proof](#proof-stmt-fill-cubical-2): Use uniform selective hyperbolicity, bounded wall collapse, sheet stability, and the cubical branched model to construct a quasiconvex hierarchy. -> claim-selective-cover-quotient
- **step-progressive-coefficient-descent** [claim](#stmt-fill-progressive) / [proof](#proof-stmt-fill-progressive): Linearize, descend maximal inverse ancestry through a normal RFRS chain, selectively embed residual supports, and recombine both signs by perturbation. -> claim-progressive-characters
- **step-rfrs-open-regions** [claim](#stmt-fill-rfrs-novikov) / [proof](#proof-stmt-fill-rfrs-novikov): Run coefficient descent without a selective switch, then truncate contractions to finite strict inequalities in character space. -> claim-open-rfrs-novikov-regions
- **step-recover-free-kernel** [claim](#stmt-fill-criterion) / [proof](#proof-stmt-fill-free-kernel-2): Apply two-sided Novikov vanishing, the degree-one BNS implication, coherence, and the dimension obstruction for finitely presented kernels. -> claim-filling-criterion
- **step-ascending-relative-model** [claim](#stmt-asc-relative-model) / [proof](#proof-stmt-asc-relative-model): Use iterated-image cores to obtain rank reduction or an irreducible equivariant homothety; analyze its real-tree point stabilizers by coarse retractions. -> claim-relative-tree-model and lower-rank quasiconvex peripherals
- **step-ascending-good-fillings** [claim](#stmt-asc-filled-vcs) / [proof](#proof-stmt-asc-filled-vcs): Avoid seed folds, pass to finite graph covers, stabilize block image ranks, and assemble primitive blocks through cyclic connector splittings. -> claim-filled-ascending-specialness
- **step-ascending-induction-fibering** [claim](#stmt-asc-vcs) / [proof](#proof-stmt-asc-filled-vcs-2): Complete every rank-induction branch, then apply RFRS contractions and the free-kernel argument to obtain the stronger virtual fibering conclusion. -> claim-ascending-specialness and claim-ascending-specialness-intro
- **step-actual-row-homology** [claim](#stmt-row-path-inertia) / [proof](#proof-stmt-row-path-inertia): Refine the Magnus splitting, establish row geometry and level bases, then restrict induced matrices over actual double cosets while extending paths. -> claim-path-inertia
- **step-row-gates-periodicity** [claim](#stmt-row-period-rule) / [proof](#proof-stmt-row-period-rule): Combine finite row homology with height-periodic Mayer–Vietoris data and the subtree gate criterion. -> claim-period-rule
- **step-algebraic-support-descent** [claim](#stmt-coeff-support) / [proof](#proof-stmt-coeff-extraction-2): Induct on hereditary ordinal complexity to separate disjoint permitted supports, extend a scalar functional, and use rational descent and separability for coset spans. -> claim-support-coset-descent
- **step-affiliated-localization** [claim](#stmt-coeff-analytic-support) / [proof](#proof-stmt-coeff-analytic-mean-2): Use measure calculus and spectral comparisons to construct a tight positive mean, unitarize the compressed transport, and eliminate infinite coset orbits by finite module dimension. -> claim-semilinear-affiliated-support
- **step-expansion-and-persistence** [claim](#stmt-gate-phase-uniqueness) / [proof](#proof-stmt-gate-phase-uniqueness): Bound core comparisons, derive corridor flaring, control cyclic index changes, and pull expanding periods back to rule out late divergence. -> claim-phase-uniqueness
- **step-periodic-tail-switch-data** [claim](#stmt-gate-local-switch-tree) / [proof](#proof-stmt-gate-local-switch-tree): Approximate decreasing cores, extract periodic branching states, prove active tails noncyclic, and identify deep-window color trees. -> claim-local-switch-tree
- **step-switch-components-and-capture** [claim](#stmt-gate-capture) / [proof](#proof-stmt-gate-capture): Control coarsening orbits and incident free factors; use the proper-free-quotient obstruction to exclude circuits and jointly inject captured kernels. -> claim-periodic-path-capture
- **step-cyclic-join-closure** [claim](#stmt-close-strict-system) / [proof](#proof-stmt-close-strict-system): Exclude cyclic incidence circuits, calculate component homology, retain detection, and prove joint injection before terminating horizontal and positive-height joins separately. -> claim-finite-strict-closure
- **step-strict-row-folding** [claim](#stmt-close-folding) / [proof](#proof-stmt-close-folding): Use root closure and raw jump support, correct root cylinders, exclude folded incidence circuits, and restrict folded slot sequences. -> claim-strict-folded-tree
- **step-end-enlargement-terminal-system** [claim](#stmt-close-terminal-system) / [proof](#proof-stmt-close-terminal-system): Inject tail and end homology, split full tail factors, prove end specialness through virtually free fillings, and use strict budget growth to terminate enlargement. -> claim-terminal-periodic-system
- **step-unfilled-relative-geometry** [claim](#stmt-transfer-relative-rows) / [proof](#proof-stmt-transfer-relative-rows): Capture fixed rays and bound peripheral incidences; glue relative actual-row models and prove partial-metric hyperbolicity. -> claim-relative-row-geometry
- **step-relative-windows-terminal-bound** [claim](#stmt-transfer-terminal-paths) / [proof](#proof-stmt-transfer-terminal-paths): Use unfilled comparisons, exact intersections, and finite double-coset lists to verify the relative expansion package and rule out unbounded nonparabolic windows. -> claim-terminal-path-bound
- **step-exact-filling-intersections** [claim](#stmt-transfer-exact-intersection) / [proof](#proof-stmt-transfer-exact-intersection): Fix original dictionaries and compatible peripheral tests, establish induced injections, then concatenate strip lifts using shared connector representatives. -> claim-exact-intersection-transfer
- **step-filled-paths-ambient-quasiconvexity** [claim](#stmt-transfer-finite-path-transfer) / [proof](#proof-stmt-transfer-finite-path-transfer): Recurse through finite path representatives, transfer stabilizers exactly, derive acylindricity, and use normalized coset projections to retract onto rows. -> claim-finite-path-filling-transfer with ambient quasiconvexity
- **step-local-cones-and-characters** [claim](#stmt-kernel-characters) / [proof](#proof-stmt-kernel-characters): Build field-contractible local cones, obtain Novikov openness, arrange visible independent evaluations and finite cyclic separation, then choose a conjugation-closed integral family. -> claim-generic-integral-characters
- **step-exact-height-fiber-kernels** [claim](#stmt-kernel-construction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-kernel-construction): Specialize scalar contractions, propagate level cohomology, intersect nontrivial-mode annihilators, and verify exact graph covers and cyclic orders simultaneously. -> claim-simultaneous-compatible-kernels
- **step-fan-and-central-panels** [claim](#stmt-fan-sparse-panels) / [proof](#proof-stmt-fan-sparse-panels): Develop central component presentations and tagged filled fans; combine finite angle dictionaries, exact covers, and marker comparison with sparse potential tests. -> claim-sparse-central-panels
- **step-central-trees-odd-seeds** [claim](#stmt-fan-odd-seeds) / [proof](#proof-stmt-fan-odd-seeds): Match cuts to slots, define closed central cochains, prove arm exclusivity, and preserve winding through even replacements to produce odd seeds. -> claim-odd-satellite-seeds
- **step-complete-wall-cocycles** [claim](#stmt-boundary-completed-trees) / [proof](#proof-stmt-boundary-completed-trees): Use nonmixed profiles and equivariant odd-side consumption to build internal trees; pair outer odd encounters and extend cocycles across all fans. -> claim-completed-wall-trees and claim-cocycle-boundary-sides
- **step-boundary-parity-separation** [claim](#stmt-boundary-separation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-boundary-separation): Normalize bounded outer turns, test satellite and central parities, and preserve an odd horizontal edge in the regular case; treat large internal and outer turns separately. -> claim-full-boundary-separation
- **step-good-vertices-and-quotients** [claim](#stmt-boundary-good-fillings) / [proof](#proof-stmt-boundary-good-fillings): Fix scales without circular dependence, cubulate filled vertices using boundary separators, then assemble their ambient quasiconvex hierarchy. -> claim-arbitrarily-deep-good-quotients
- **step-primitive-and-main-conclusions** [claim](#stmt-boundary-primitive-vcs) / [proof](#proof-stmt-boundary-primitive-vcs): Check the primitive finiteness and field prerequisites, apply the filling criterion, then propagate through the truncated tower and obtain the finite Salvetti model. -> claim-primitive-extension-specialness and claim-one-relator-specialness
- **step-virtual-free-by-cyclic-consequences** [claim](#stmt-cor-free-by-cyclic) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-free-by-cyclic): Apply the stated compact-special virtual fibering and embedding results, then intersect the embedded subgroup with the ambient free kernel. -> claim-virtual-free-by-cyclic-embedding

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-compact-special-model**: The one-relator conclusion includes a compact special finite-cover model and a cubical local isometry to a finite Salvetti complex.
- **invariant-ascending-finite-rank-fibering**: A hyperbolic ascending torus of an injective finite-rank free-group endomorphism has a finite-index subgroup with finite-rank free kernel and infinite cyclic quotient.
- **invariant-actual-path-homology**: Actual path stabilizers inject jointly on first field homology, including after subgroup restriction; the numerical rank budget alone does not replace this injection.
- **invariant-exact-intersection-transfer**: Sufficiently long compatible fillings preserve the exact intersection of the fixed embedded subgroups, using embedded standalone subgroup fillings.
- **invariant-local-cover-equality**: The height-fiber kernel restricts to exactly the local annihilator intersection, giving equality with the prescribed graph cover.
- **invariant-general-free-kernel-scope**: The general virtual free-by-cyclic conclusion permits an infinite-rank free kernel and a trivial cyclic image; only the ambient embedding has an asserted finite-rank free kernel.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-abstract-embedding-as-compact-model**: Treat an abstract embedding of a finite-index subgroup in a right-angled Artin group as the full compact-special conclusion. -> The embedding alone does not provide the required compact cubical model.
- **anti-finite-rank-general-kernel**: Represent the general free kernel by a finite free basis merely because the ambient free-by-cyclic group has a finite-rank free kernel. -> A subgroup of the ambient free group need not be finitely generated.
- **anti-canonical-height-identification**: Identify the finite-rank fibering character with the original ascending height. -> The virtual fibering conclusion does not identify these homomorphisms.
- **anti-finite-generation-for-quasiconvexity**: Apply quasiconvex subgroup separability or virtual retraction to an arbitrary finitely generated subgroup. -> The cited application requires quasiconvexity.
- **anti-uncontrolled-kernel-refinement**: Intersect the final height-fiber kernel with an arbitrary further finite-index subgroup and retain the exact local cover claim. -> Additional intersections can destroy the exact restriction identity that defines the local covers.
- **anti-relative-package-by-default**: Transfer ordinary expansion and phase uniqueness directly to relative rows. -> Passing to relative rows does not automatically preserve the expansion package.
- **anti-computational-certificate-for-existence**: Treat finite examples of graph covers or matrix identities as a certificate of the full virtual compact specialness theorem. -> Such checks do not establish the global existence arguments, infinite subgroup chains, or affiliated-operator localization.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The main results establish global existence of finite-index compact-special models and virtual fibrations, rather than a finite executable construction with supplied input witnesses and effective stopping bounds. A source-bound obstruction occurs in the support argument: “Define a linear functional on $W+\mathbb Q1$ by $\ell(w+q)=q$, and extend it to a $\mathbb Q$-linear functional on $D_J$.” The affiliated positive mean also treats an infinite family of affiliated operators under tightness assumptions. Finite checks of isolated matrix identities or graph covers would certify only those instances, not these global proof obligations.

| domain | applies | strength | maturity | basis | why |

| software | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The compact special model is an existence conclusion. The paper does not specify a software interface that constructs that model from an input presentation. |
| games_simulation | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The tree and cubical constructions describe group geometry; the paper provides no simulation state, update rule, or gameplay construction. |
| tools | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The peripheral compatibility tests are mathematical conditions on subgroup occurrences and fillings. A general procedure deciding those conditions from finite input is not supplied. |
| algorithms | True | moderate | adaptable | inferred | Controlled linearization supplies a finite recursive construction on rational expressions: polynomial inputs receive triangular matrix representations, sums use block diagonals, products use triangular blocks, and inverses use bordered matrices. This supports a symbolic transformation once the coefficient operations and admissibility of the inverse operands are established. |
| data_structures | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | Actual subgroup frames and induced-module decompositions are essential bookkeeping in the proof, but the paper does not give an operational storage or query contract for them. |
| hardware_accelerators | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The affiliated-operator argument establishes convergence and tightness in an infinite-dimensional algebraic setting. It supplies no finite hardware representation or accelerator construction. |
| crypto_security | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | Residual finiteness and conjugacy separability concern distinguishing elements or conjugacy classes in finite quotients. They provide neither a cryptographic construction nor a hardness assumption. |
| machine_learning | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The generic character family is chosen to avoid algebraic rank drops and vanishing evaluations. It is not a learning model, training procedure, or statistical prediction contract. |
| optimisation_operations_research | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The homology budget controls admissibility and termination of closure operations. The paper specifies no optimisation objective or procedure for finding a best peripheral system. |
| distributed_systems | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | Equivariant consumption coordinates mathematical incidences under a group action. It does not construct a distributed protocol with message, failure, or consistency semantics. |
| other | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The principal additional relevance is to geometric group theory and topology. The virtual embedding conclusion does not itself specify an additional engineering construction. |

<a id="pm-s6"></a>
## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-hyperbolic-one-relator-scope** (hypothesis): The main compact-special conclusion requires a finite generating set, a single relator, and word-hyperbolicity. Blocked use: ['Apply the main theorem to an arbitrary nonhyperbolic presentation or an unrestricted finitely presented group.']
- **limit-compact-model-not-abstract-embedding** (formal_scope): An abstract embedding in a right-angled Artin group does not supply the required compact cubical model. Blocked use: ['Record an abstract subgroup embedding as a complete compact-special witness.']
- **limit-ascending-input** (hypothesis): The ascending specialness theorem requires an injective endomorphism of a finite-rank free group and a word-hyperbolic mapping torus. Blocked use: ['Apply the ascending conclusion to a noninjective presentation endomorphism without establishing an applicable stable-image reduction.', 'Replace the hyperbolicity hypothesis by a weaker geometric assumption.']
- **limit-filling-criterion-joint-prerequisites** (hypothesis): The filling criterion requires the full package of coherence, local indicability, finiteness, cohomological dimension, subgroup-field acyclicity, and good peripheral fillings. Blocked use: ['Recover virtual specialness from the existence of some good quotients while omitting the remaining hypotheses.']
- **limit-special-quotient-containment** (hypothesis): Finite avoidance does not replace containment in the designated normal subgroups used by the special quotient theorem. Blocked use: ['Declare a peripheral filling suitable solely because it avoids a finite set.']
- **limit-selective-quotient-retained-factors** (hypothesis): Selective preservation concerns the prescribed finite family of kernel factors after the stated finite-index preimage refinement. Blocked use: ['Claim simultaneous injectivity on the entire filling kernel from preservation of a finite selected subproduct.', 'Omit invariance of the retained factor set under the refined subgroup.']
- **limit-sheet-stabilizers-not-free-action** (edge_case): Positive-dimensional sheets have free deck action, while vertex-sheet stabilizers can contain whole retained factors. Blocked use: ['Infer a proper action of the selective quotient on the branched cubical model from cocompactness alone.', 'Treat every sheet stabilizer as trivial.']
- **limit-linearization-admissible-inverses** (hypothesis): Controlled linearization represents rational expressions in a specified division ring; it does not decide whether arbitrary proposed inverse operands are admissible. Blocked use: ['Turn the block construction into a general decision procedure for nonvanishing or equality in arbitrary division rings.']
- **limit-descent-depth-relative-to-kernel-field** (formal_scope): Termination at inverse depth zero relative to the kernel division ring can leave unresolved division-field coefficients. Blocked use: ['Treat the first quotient-chain descent as already producing ordinary group-ring coefficients.']
- **limit-recombination-both-signs-and-support** (hypothesis): Character recombination requires compatible realizations of the scalar coefficients for both signs and perturbations small enough to preserve the positive error valuations. Blocked use: ['Recombine from a realization available for only one sign.', 'Ignore homogeneous support or finite-index coordinate offsets when perturbing characters.']
- **limit-free-kernel-finite-presentation** (hypothesis): The dimension argument for freeness assumes a finitely presented kernel; finite generation alone is supplied to that argument through coherence. Blocked use: ['Apply the free-kernel lemma directly to an arbitrary finitely generated kernel without its finite-presentation hypothesis.']
- **limit-primitive-exceptional-data** (hypothesis): The primitive presentations include the stated slot exclusions, torsion-free hyperbolicity, malnormality, and exceptional-factorization qualifications. Blocked use: ['Apply primitive-row conclusions to every substituted positive primitive word merely because its presentation has the displayed general shape.']
- **limit-actual-frames-and-joint-injection** (formal_scope): Actual subgroup occurrences and subgroup-restricted joint homology injections must be retained; an abstract subgroup type or numerical rank budget does not replace them. Blocked use: ['Merge distinct conjugating frames because their stabilizers are abstractly isomorphic.', 'Use only the rank inequality when subsequent arguments distinguish orbit summands.']
- **limit-period-rule-finite-generation** (hypothesis): The period rule obtains the finite quotient and ambient quasiconvexity conclusion only with the additional finite-generation hypothesis on the periodic subgroup. Blocked use: ['Deduce ambient quasiconvexity solely from positive finite kernel homology and nonzero height.']
- **limit-finite-span-separability** (hypothesis): The finite-span descent assertion requires the subgroup intersection to be separable in both groups. Blocked use: ['Apply the finite-span intersection equality using only the single-coset descent assertion.']
- **limit-scalar-map-not-multiplicative** (formal_scope): The scalar-function map preserves linear equations and right group translations; multiplicativity for division-ring coefficients is not asserted. Blocked use: ['Replace a product of arbitrary division-ring coefficients by the pointwise product of their scalar-function images.']
- **limit-scalar-functional-extension** (nonconstructive): The support proof extends a linear functional beyond its initially specified subspace without giving a finite evaluation procedure for the extension. Blocked use: ['Treat the scalar-function existence argument as executable coefficient extraction on arbitrary division-ring elements.']
- **limit-affiliated-localization-assumptions** (hypothesis): Semilinear localization requires quasiconvexity, matching nonzero heights, affiliated realizations, and the stated invertible coefficient relation. Blocked use: ['Infer finite periodic-coset support for an arbitrary affiliated row without the semilinear relation or quasiconvex subgroup.']
- **limit-affiliated-mean-infinite-input** (nonconstructive): The affiliated positive mean concerns an infinite family and requires tightness of both the inputs and their inverses. Blocked use: ['Replace the infinite mean equation by an unchecked finite sample.', 'Assume tightness of the inputs alone suffices.']
- **limit-relative-expansion-package** (hypothesis): The relative expansion argument is conditional on the complete expansion package. Blocked use: ['Transfer ordinary flaring or phase uniqueness to relative rows without verifying exact peripheral restrictions, finite-window geometry, and competing-continuation intersections.']
- **limit-decreasing-tail-versus-end-homology** (edge_case): General pointwise tail groups are asserted to have finite-dimensional ambiently injected homology; positivity is separately asserted for the end kernels. Blocked use: ['Assign positive field homology to every pointwise tail stabilizer solely from the joint-tail lemma.']
- **limit-horizontal-closure-stationarity** (formal_scope): The budget increase controls positive-height joins; horizontal joins require the separate finite-generation stationarity argument. Blocked use: ['Claim that every cyclic-closure round strictly increases the homology budget.', 'Use the budget alone as a bound on all closure rounds.']
- **limit-folding-equivalence** (formal_scope): Strict folding identifies equal-height points through the specified object subtrees and their transitive equivalence. Blocked use: ['Identify all equal-height points of the actual tree without reference to the object subtrees.']
- **limit-exact-relative-not-full** (formal_scope): Exact relative embeddings use the actual induced peripheral intersections and do not require every induced subgroup to equal its ambient peripheral. Blocked use: ['Replace an induced cyclic intersection by a full peripheral subgroup.', 'Identify different actual peripheral cosets based only on subgroup conjugacy type.']
- **limit-filling-tests-order-and-exactness** (hypothesis): Exact intersection transfer requires the specified original compatibility requests, including product membership and exact peripheral intersections, fixed before choosing sufficiently long filling kernels. Blocked use: ['Infer exact subgroup-intersection preservation from ordinary relative filling alone.', 'Choose unrelated lifts of a shared connector in adjacent comparison strips.']
- **limit-finite-path-transfer-range** (formal_scope): Finite-path lifting is asserted for the fixed tested length and infinite stabilizers; acylindricity yields uniformly bounded finite stabilizers rather than necessarily trivial ones. Blocked use: ['Claim exact lifting for every finite stabilizer or every untested path length.', 'Replace acylindricity by freeness of the filled tree action.']
- **limit-local-cover-final-kernel** (hypothesis): The exact local cover description belongs to the constructed annihilator kernel and need not survive an arbitrary later finite-index intersection. Blocked use: ['Refine the final kernel arbitrarily while continuing to assert equality with the prescribed local cover.']
- **limit-scalar-specialization-nontrivial-modes** (hypothesis): Scalar specialization uses the chosen odd prime, a finite field of different characteristic containing the required roots of unity, and nontrivial deck characters. Blocked use: ['Apply the local twisted-cohomology isomorphism to the trivial deck mode without separate justification.', 'Use a coefficient characteristic incompatible with the cyclic deck decomposition.']
- **limit-tagged-fans-not-embedded-boundaries** (formal_scope): Satellite and outer word paths retain occurrence tags even when their physical vertices or edges repeat. Blocked use: ['Discard occurrence tags or assume each boundary word is an embedded physical cycle.']
- **limit-marker-gluing-endpoint-conditions** (hypothesis): The marker gluing conclusion requires distinct endpoint markers, avoidance of those markers inside connectors, unique attachment at a marker, and sufficiently separated spoke germs. Blocked use: ['Conclude that a collection of quasiconvex tree pieces remains a tree merely because individual switch angles are large.']
- **limit-nonmixed-panels-and-consumption** (hypothesis): Satellite-only panels have no central labels and consume an even number of odd sides on each arm; equivariant copying accounts for each odd side exactly once. Blocked use: ['Combine central and satellite labels at the same total panel without redoing the contamination argument.', 'Pair odd sides without checking arm parity or equivariant multiplicities.']
- **limit-boundary-color-domain** (hypothesis): Boundary cocycle colors are defined outside the tree limit set, and separation requires different colors there. Blocked use: ['Use an odd path evaluation as boundary separation without proving that both ideal endpoints avoid the tree limit set.']
- **limit-finite-choice-order** (formal_scope): Later angle, girth, period-order, and kernel choices must follow the finite dependency order established by the construction. Blocked use: ['Feed stronger later cut thresholds back into earlier class bounds and assume the resulting parameter choice remains noncircular.']
- **limit-general-free-kernel-rank** (edge_case): The general virtual free-by-cyclic conclusion permits an infinite-rank free kernel and a trivial cyclic image. Blocked use: ['Require a finite free basis for the general subgroup kernel.', 'Assert that the general subgroup necessarily maps onto an infinite cyclic group.']
- **limit-fibering-character-not-canonical-height** (formal_scope): The finite-rank virtual fibering character of an ascending torus is not identified with its canonical ascending height. Blocked use: ['Infer finite generation of the canonical height kernel from the existence of the virtual fibering character.']
- **limit-subgroup-quasiconvexity-and-largeness** (hypothesis): The subgroup separation application retains quasiconvexity, and the largeness conclusion additionally requires non-elementarity. Blocked use: ['Apply virtual retractions to arbitrary finitely generated subgroups.', 'Claim largeness for every elementary group covered by the main theorem.']
- **limit-effective-global-construction-absent** (unknown): Explicit global runtime, storage, and finite-cover index bounds are ABSENT. Blocked use: ['Advertise a complexity guarantee or practical cover-size bound from the global existence theorems.', 'Treat finite checks of local identities as certification of the entire geometric argument.']

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


We prove that every word-hyperbolic one-relator group is virtually compact special. Combined with the work of Kielak–Linton, this resolves Wise's virtual free-by-cyclic conjecture for hyperbolic one-relator groups: every such group is virtually free-by-cyclic, with the free kernel allowed to have infinite rank.
